DhSettings.title: Character settings

DhSettings.name: Name

forceDiceLook.name: Dice look for the table
forceDiceLook.hint: With one look, players and Assistant GMs throw in one full Gamemaster's Dice So Nice look, fixed the first time the game runs with it on. The Daggerheart look adds Daggerheart's Hope and Despair colors.

forcePrivateRolls.name: Force private player rolls
forcePrivateRolls.hint: Every player roll is whispered to that player and the GMs, a GM's roll to the GMs. Only a GM's game.drpg.publicRoll macro is seen by all.

enforceAnonymity.name: Keep character sheets anonymous
enforceAnonymity.hint: Another player's sheet shows only their name, portrait, Ultimate, Health, what they hold, and how many Experiences they have. Each player's own sheet stays whole.

searchTokensPerRoom.name: Search Tokens per room
searchTokensPerRoom.hint: Search Tokens per room each time of day, 0 to 10. A Search uses one; a room with none left cannot be searched.

lockRollDialog.name: Lock the roll window for players
lockRollDialog.hint: Players cannot change the dice, statistic, advantage, experiences, or bonus in the roll window; those come from the action, a Hope Call or the GM. GMs are unaffected.

roomVisibility.name: Players only see who is in their room
roomVisibility.hint: Hides other characters unless they stand in the same room, through gaps in the walls too. GMs see everything.

isoTokenShield.name: Guard token editing from Isometric Perspective
isoTokenShield.hint: Keeps the isometric-perspective module out of the token configuration window, where it breaks editing. Turn it off to reach its Isometric tab.

regionFog.name: Rooms decide what players can see
regionFog.hint: A player sees their own room; visited rooms show through, the rest is fogged.

lockPlayerResources.name: Lock players' resources on the sheet
lockPlayerResources.hint: Actions, Hope, Health, Sanity, and statistics change only through play. On, a player's own edits of them are put back or flagged to the GMs; off, they are only listed. Items and effects are checked either way. GMs are unaffected.

autoApproveTraits.name: Players' statistics without approval
autoApproveTraits.hint: A player's statistic for a Search or a project goes through without your click. Resolve asks nobody.

friskForce.name: Frisk: forcing after a refusal
friskForce.hint: When off, an open Frisk only asks: a refusal or no answer ends it.

chargeMovement.name: Crossing rooms costs a Move
chargeMovement.hint: Moving inside a room is free. The first crossing each time of day uses the Free Move; later ones cost an action or a Sprint crossing. Off, you handle movement yourself.

despairFromRolls.name: Rolls grant Despair
despairFromRolls.hint: A roll that lands with Despair feeds the pool of that student's Monokuma. Divide the students up in GM panel, Despair Flow.

hideSystemFear.name: Replace the Daggerheart Fear tracker
hideSystemFear.hint: Hides Daggerheart's single shared Fear bar and gives every Monokuma a Despair pool of their own. Turn off to go back to the system tracker.

enforceIsoWelcome.name: Keep Isometric Perspective's welcome window closed for everyone
enforceIsoWelcome.hint: Isometric Perspective's welcome window opens for nobody.

enforceDhWelcome.name: Keep Daggerheart's welcome window closed for everyone
enforceDhWelcome.hint: Daggerheart's welcome journal opens for nobody, the GM included.

enforcePlayerFiles.name: Keep players out of the file browser
enforcePlayerFiles.hint: Players cannot browse or upload files, and a click on a portrait opens nothing. Pictures already in the world still show.

liveKitInFoundry.name: Voice inside the Foundry window for everyone
liveKitInFoundry.hint: Voice runs in the Foundry window, with no separate tab.

pixelFont.name: Pixel font
pixelFont.hint: Monokuma Legacy only: Press Start 2P on the HUD, tabs, names, and labels. Long text keeps the normal face.

language.name: Language
language.hint: The language of this module's windows, cards, and sheet; Foundry keeps its own. Game names such as Truth Bullet stay in English. Needs a reload. Only affects this browser.

documentLanguage.name: Document language
documentLanguage.hint: The language of the documents the module writes into this world, one for everyone. Windows, cards, and the sheet stay in the Language each browser sets. Set by the primary GM's first start, to their language.

moveAudit.name: A player's token moved through a wall
moveAudit.hint: When someone moves a player's token through a wall.
moveAudit.log: Note it in the Debug log

foundryToolWindows.name: The module's windows for Foundry's sidebar and scene controls
foundryToolWindows.hint: The sidebar and map tools in two windows, from the button in the corner.

glassPulse.name: Glass pulse
glassPulse.hint: The slow darkening that travels around the frame. Turn it off to keep the glass and stop it breathing. This client only.

highContrast.name: High contrast
highContrast.hint: Brighter fine print, solid hairlines, opaque panels and no blur behind the chrome. Text sizes belong to the Interface scale rather than to this switch, and the map is left alone. On by itself when your system asks for more contrast. This client only.

sequences.name: Full-screen sequences
sequences.hint: The Class Trial's entry, the verdict, the clock's turns and flashes, and the day boards, on every screen. Off, only the trial's and the verdict's sounds play. Esc skips one.

reducedMotion.name: Reduced motion
reducedMotion.hint: Hold the interface still on this browser, whatever the operating system says. This client only.

hudTicker.name: State name behind the clock
hudTicker.hint: The time of day, faint, behind the clock.

bulletSort.name: How Truth Bullets are grouped
bulletSort.hint: Sorts your Truth Bullets by chapter, the default, or by room. The switch is in your inventory, beside them. Only affects this browser.

glassBlur.name: Glass blurs the map
glassBlur.hint: The glass frosts the map behind it. If the game stutters, turn this off first.

messengerSound.name: Messenger sounds
messengerSound.hint: The three sounds the messenger plays - sent, received, a question for the GM. Only affects this browser.

uiScale.name: Interface scale
uiScale.hint: The size of the module's windows and text, and with them Foundry's own and the sheet, 80% to 140%. The map is not scaled. Only affects this browser.

debug.name: Verbose console logging
debug.hint: Print Danganronpa RPG diagnostics to the browser console. Only affects this browser.

musicEnabled.name: Music follows the game state
musicEnabled.hint: Changes the playlist with the game: an Eclipse, a trial, an investigation, the time of day, a pause. Map the playlists first in the Sound window.

voiceEnabled.name: Separate voice in each room
voiceEnabled.hint: You hear only the people in your room. Needs LiveKit AVClient.

voiceTile.name: Voice tile instead of the camera dock
voiceTile.hint: Hides the cameras. The tile shows how many people are in your channel.

why.noScene: the scene it was on is gone. Propose it again on a scene that stands.
why.twoRooms: the stretch does not join two rooms. Pick a stretch on a wall between two rooms.
why.gmOnly: only a GM's browser can do this. Ask it again from a GM's.
why.noStore: the GMs' record of this season's passages is not loaded. Reload the world, then take a point off the project and finish it again.
why.noBuilder: its builder is no longer a student of this world. Make a new project for another student if it should still happen.
why.idTaken: another passage took its place at the same moment. Take a point off the project and finish it again.
why.breached: that wall already has a breach. Close that breach first, or pick another wall.
why.wholeWall: the stretch takes the whole wall, and nothing of it would stand. Pick a shorter stretch.
why.noBreach: that breach is no longer there: a GM or another project closed it first. Nothing is left to do.
why.wallGone: the wall it was cut from is gone. The room beyond is given back; delete the hole by hand with the walls tool.
why.cannotClose: the passage could not be closed. Close it by hand in the Passages tab.
why.notKnown: the character does not know that passage, or it is closed already. Check it in the Passages tab.
why.isBreach: that is a breach, not a passage. Close the breach gives the wall back.
why.noSide: it has no side in the room where the character stands. Approve it only from a room the passage or the breach opens into.
why.lockWhole: that lock is not broken - nothing to repair.
why.lockTaken: a project repairs that lock already.
why.lockFar: that lock is on no door of the room where the character stands. Approve it only from that room or one next to it.
why.noWall: the wall is gone. Pick the stretch again.
why.taken: the stretch overlaps another passage on that wall. Pick a stretch beside it.
why.levels: a room beside the stretch is on another floor. Pick a stretch on the character's floor.
why.notBetween: the stretch does not stand between two rooms. Pick a stretch of a wall between two rooms.
why.otherRooms: the stretch's two ends stand between different rooms. Pick both ends between the same two rooms.
why.short: the stretch is too short. Pick a longer stretch.
why.door: that wall is a door. Pick a stretch of a solid wall.
why.noMove: that wall does not stop anyone. Pick a stretch of a solid wall.
why.sameEnds: the stretch needs two different ends. Pick it again.
why.offWall: the stretch is no longer on that wall. Pick it again.
why.floor: that wall is not on the character's floor. Pick a wall of that floor.
why.notOwn: the item is not on the builder's own sheet: given away, taken, or a shared sheet's. Approve a repair only for an item the character holds.
why.notRepairable: the item is no usable or tool, or it is whole already. There is nothing to repair.
why.nothingBack: there is nothing to put back. Cut the breach again by hand if it should stand.
why.itemBack: there was nothing to put back on the item.
why.brokenSince: the item was broken or worn again since, and is left as it is.
why.repairTooSmall: the item's tier went up since this repair was approved, so nothing was mended. Approve a new repair of the right size.
why.unknown: the module could not say why; the reason is in the GM's console.

murderWitness.other: {n} people besides your victim are in the room and would see it, so the attempt fails. The action stays spent; try again at another time of day.

Action.searchTokensLeft: {left} of {max} Search Tokens left in this room.

Monocub.cannotMeddle: Not enough action, or not enough Hope.
Monocub.mustBeDead: Only a character who has already died becomes a Monocub.
Monocub.onlyTwoActions: A Monocub moves freely and uses its own tiles: Confusion, Tinker, Redeem, Ask for Hope and Ghost Bet.
Monocub.opted: {name} has joined the GMs as a Monocub.
Monocub.dialogIntro: After their own Class Trial, a dead player can join as a Monocub.
Monocub.giveHope: Turn a Monokuma's Despair into Hope
Monocub.giveAtLeast: Type how much Despair to turn into Hope - at least {n}.
Monocub.silencedNote: Ticked by itself when this Monocub is in the room of a murder. Tick it if they saw the crime some other way. They can't discuss it until the chapter ends; Confusion still works.
Monocub.needHope: Confusion costs Hope and you have none. Ask a GM to convert some Despair.
Monocub.nobodyHere: Nobody in this room to use Confusion on.

Monocub.grantAdvantage: advantage with Help, disadvantage with Hinder, on their next roll

Monocub.noProjectHere: No project in this room to use Tinker on.
Monocub.grantStep: the project one step forward with Help, back with Hinder
Monocub.tinkerHeld: Tinker: {name} holds one step short of done. Somebody living has to finish it.

bountyOwedCancelled.other: The {n} Despair {pool} owed for it is cancelled.

flag.third: A third Bribe this chapter between {name} and {cub}.

Monocub.critHinderNothingTarget: A moment's confusion, but you had no action left to lose.

Monocub.wrongVerdictTold: Told the verdict let the killer go: {names}.
Monocub.inviteIntro: The GMs invite {name} back as a Monocub: you keep playing from the sidelines, with Confusion, Tinker, Redeem and Ask for Hope.

Monocub.darkened: The darkening blocks Hope this time of day.

Monocub.moveRefused: That move doesn't go through now. You keep your action and Hope.
Monocub.askNotNowTold: Your Ask for Hope: not now. You can ask again.

Mastermind.finalRunningNote: This trial is the Final Trial.
Mastermind.privacyWarning: This screen names the Mastermind. Do not share your view while it is open.
Mastermind.dialogIntro: Pick them before the season starts, with that player's agreement.
Mastermind.noneSet: No Mastermind set. Pick one from the GM panel first.
Mastermind.toggleFinalTrial: Start or end the Final Trial
Mastermind.confirmStart: Start the Final Trial? Everyone at the table sees it announced.
Mastermind.confirmEnd: End the Final Trial? The table is not told, and nothing already done changes.
Mastermind.finalTruthPlaced: A Final Truth Remnant has already been placed this chapter.

Mastermind.confirmed: {name} is the Mastermind. Only the GMs and {name}'s player know.

Mastermind.finalPickRoom: Pick a room to place it

Floor.nobodyForTrial: There is nobody alive to hold a Class Trial with.
Floor.newTrialConfirm: This chapter already has a verdict. Open a new trial? A second verdict means another execution and another round of Level Ups.
Floor.newTrialRefused: This chapter already has a verdict, so the Class Trial was not opened again. A second trial opens from Start the Class Trial, which asks first.
Floor.eclipseFirst: An Eclipse is running, so nothing was opened. End the Eclipse first.
Floor.nowMovedOn: The turn had already moved on, so Skip changed nothing. Press it again if this turn should still end.
Floor.incidentOpen: A murder incident is still open. Its Blackened go on the register only when it is closed, and the vote and the verdict read the register. Close it now, or go on with it open?
Floor.registerEmpty: The Blackened register is empty, and a student died this chapter. Was the incident closed? A killer goes on the register when their incident closes.
Floor.startTrialIntro: A Class Trial opens in discussion: everybody talks, and evidence goes on the table without taking the floor. The Nonstop Debate is something you open inside it.
Floor.startTrialStepPhase: The campaign moves to Class Trial.
Floor.startTrialStepAnnounce: The trial is announced in chat and the music follows.

trialBudget.one: {n} student has this time of day's actions for the trial.
trialBudget.other: {n} students have this time of day's actions for the trial.

Floor.trialOpened: The Class Trial is in session. Talk it through; the debate opens when the GM says so.
Floor.endTrialConfirm: This closes the debate, ends the Class Trial and returns the campaign to Daily Life.
Floor.endTrialNotChapter: The chapter is not ended - use End the chapter for the reveal and the next chapter.
Floor.endTrialExecutes: Ending the trial carries out the sentence: {names}.
Floor.endTrialScene: The living students who took part go to the room you choose here, from whichever scene with rooms they stand on; a student who cannot be moved stays where they stood and you are told who. Floor.trialEnded: The Class Trial has ended; the chapter has not.

lead.start: No Class Trial is running. Start the Class Trial: the phase moves, the table is told, and the trial opens in discussion.
lead.openDebate: The trial is in discussion. Open the debate when the room is ready to argue; when it has argued it out, send the ballots from The vote.
lead.openAgain: The GM overruled an Objection after its exchange, and the trial is in discussion. Open the debate again with the time it had left, or send the ballots from The vote.
lead.reopen: The exchange has closed the debate, and the trial is in discussion. Open the debate again with the same question and budget, or send the ballots from The vote.
lead.closeDebate: The debate is open. Close it when the room has argued it out, then send the ballots from The vote.
lead.now: An objection or a rebuttal holds the floor. It runs out on its own; Skip on the bar cuts it short.
lead.vote: The ballots are out. When they are back, Close and count in The vote.
lead.verdict: The vote is counted. Deliver the verdict, then end the chapter.

diag.clock: Clock: phase={phase} time of day={time} eclipse={eclipse} paused={paused}
diag.cueMissing: MISSING - the Play button has nothing to draw from
diag.onCue: {name} - the cue playlist, never played for a state
diag.noState: No state applies at all - nothing will play.
diag.unmapped: "{state}" is the active state but has no playlist to play, so the music is left alone. Map one: GM panel, Sound, Music.

Cleanup.title: Cleaning up
Cleanup.intro: Each attempt costs {n} Sanity, hit or miss; the first after a critical Finishing Blow costs none.
Cleanup.priceGone: Hiding what you were doing took your last Sanity, so this attempt stops here; that Sanity stays spent.
Cleanup.keptSanity: The Sanity stays spent: you already rolled to hide what you were doing.
Cleanup.withTool: With “{item}” (Tier {tier}) in hand, you roll with advantage, and the number to beat to erase or reshape drops by {tier}.
Cleanup.bareHands: You hold no tool, so you clean with bare hands, without advantage.
Cleanup.noneReadied: No Cleaning Tool readied. One gives advantage and lowers the number to erase; hold one ready on the Inventory tab.

blocked.noIncident: No incident is running, so there is nothing to clean up.
blocked.notYet: The incident is still going on. You can clean up once it is over.
blocked.notYours: Only the killer can clean up this crime scene.
blocked.monokuma: A Monokuma does not clean up after a killing.

Cleanup.trailNobody: There is nobody left to frame.
Cleanup.moveHint: Spend {n} Sanity and roll Body to drag the body to a connected room. If it moves, you leave an Evident Remnant.
Cleanup.bodyNotHere: The body is not in this room. You have to be with it to move it.
Cleanup.nothingHere: There is no Remnant to erase in this room.
Cleanup.allReinforced: Every Remnant here is Reinforced and cannot be erased or reshaped.
Cleanup.rerollLost: A clean-up Reroll could not run: the attempt it would redo was not found, or was on another Remnant. The first roll stands, and the Hope spent on it comes back.
Cleanup.reinforced: The {what} is Reinforced and cannot be erased or reshaped.
Cleanup.vanished: The Remnant you were working on is already gone. The effort still cost you.
Cleanup.freeTonight: Cleaning up your own crime scene costs no action, only {n} Sanity per attempt; the first after a critical Finishing Blow costs none.
Cleanup.stressSpent: Each clean-up attempt costs {n} Sanity, except the first after a critical Finishing Blow.

band.failure: It will not come off, and you made a mess trying.

Cleanup.gmTool: “{item}” (Tier {tier}) is readied, so the killer rolls with advantage, and each DC below is already {tier} lower.
Cleanup.gmNoTool: The killer has no Cleaning Tool readied, so rolls without advantage.
Cleanup.gmNothingHere: No Remnants in the room the killer is standing in.

gmAttemptsLeft.one: The killer has Sanity left for {n} more attempt and can keep cleaning until it runs out or you end the murder. Ending it breaks the Murder Weapon the killer used, which stays in the inventory as Broken; the Cleaning Tool they used breaks when the body is found.
gmAttemptsLeft.other: The killer has Sanity left for {n} more attempts and can keep cleaning until it runs out or you end the murder. Ending it breaks the Murder Weapon the killer used, which stays in the inventory as Broken; the Cleaning Tool they used breaks when the body is found.

Cleanup.refundUnheld: {name}'s clean-up asked for {what} back, but no record shows it was paid, so nothing came back. If {name} did pay, give it back by hand.
Cleanup.freeAttempt: This attempt costs no Sanity: the critical Finishing Blow paid for it.
Cleanup.trailPlanted: You planted a Prep Remnant ({visibility}) pointing at {name}.
Cleanup.authorsCopy: You know this Remnant: it is on your sheet.
Cleanup.bodyStuck: The body would not move. It still lies where it fell, and you left no Remnant.
Cleanup.noBody: There is no body here to move.
Cleanup.bodyNote: {name}'s body was dragged from here to {room}.
Cleanup.seenCleaning: {actor} is doing something in {room}, and not hiding it well.
Cleanup.moveIntro: The body lies in {room}. Choose where to drag it; it costs {n} Sanity.
Cleanup.moveAlwaysTrace: You roll Body, and a Cleaning Tool in hand lowers the number. On a miss the body stays and you leave no Remnant; once it moves, it always leaves an Evident Remnant where it lay. Bedrooms are not on the list.
Cleanup.moveFar: Two rooms away, on a critical only; any other hit stops the body in the room between.
Cleanup.moveFarNote: A room two away needs a critical. Any other hit carries the body only as far as the room between.
Cleanup.bodyShort: It got only as far as {room}: {far} needed a critical.
Cleanup.bodyNowhere: There is nowhere to take the body: no room connects to this one, or only bedrooms do.
Cleanup.toolsBroken: What you used is broken and stays in your inventory: {items}.
Cleanup.transformActionHint: Rename a non-Reinforced Remnant: a GM's approval makes it a Tamper Remnant, a refusal gives nothing back.
Cleanup.transformActionIntro: Write what the next person to find this Remnant will read in its place. You pay nothing yet.
Cleanup.reshapeTextPlaceholder: A tin went over during the afternoon. Nobody cleaned it up properly.
Cleanup.reshapeNeedsBoth: Write both a name and a description. The window opens again with what you wrote.
Cleanup.reshapeNothingSaid: The reshape was missing a name or a description, so the Remnant reads as it did and the attempt is spent.
Cleanup.reshapeVoided: Taken back by a Reroll or replaced by a later attempt before {name} ruled on it.
Cleanup.reshapeTakenBack: A Reroll or a later attempt took this one's place, so this card no longer rules on anything.
Cleanup.alreadyRuled: {name} has already ruled on this reshape.
Cleanup.reshapeDeclinedErased: {name} refused your story, but your critical still erased the Remnant.
Cleanup.reshapeRulingTitle: A Remnant made to read differently
Cleanup.reshapeRulingQuieter: The roll also makes it one band harder to spot.
Cleanup.reshapeRulingTies: The student is the killer, so approving also ties the Remnant to the murder.

reshapeRulingCopies.one: If you approve, the {n} Truth Bullet already copied from it keeps the old words; whoever finds the Remnant next reads the new ones.
reshapeRulingCopies.other: If you approve, the {n} Truth Bullets already copied from it keep the old words; whoever finds the Remnant next reads the new ones.

Cleanup.reshapeWaiting: You reworked the Remnant into “{name}”. It reads as before until a GM approves.
Cleanup.reshapeDeclined: {name} refused your story, so the Remnant reads as before. The refusal gives nothing back.
Cleanup.reshapeDeclinedGm: You refused the reshape, and {name} has been told.
Cleanup.reshapeRulingGone: That Remnant is gone, so there is nothing to reshape. The player is told.
Cleanup.reshapeUnsent: A reshape card could not be sent, so nothing was written on the Remnant. If the roll was a critical Erase a Trace, the Remnant is already erased; otherwise rule on the reshape out loud, and relabel the Remnant by hand if you allow it.
Cleanup.reshapeUnsentPlayer: Your story did not reach the GM, and nothing was written on the Remnant. Tell the GM out loud.
Cleanup.reshaped: {from} now reads as “{name}” ({band} {kind}). Whoever finds it reads your story.
Cleanup.transformActionNote: A GM approves your words first, and a refusal gives nothing back. Once approved, it becomes a Tamper Remnant. A critical also makes it one band harder to spot and gives back what you paid.
Cleanup.transformIntro: Your critical lets you do more than erase this Remnant: erase it, or give it a new name and description and choose how easy it is to spot.
Cleanup.transformNote: Erasing happens now. A new story waits for a GM's approval, and then the Remnant becomes a Tamper Remnant with your words. If the GM refuses, the Remnant is erased anyway and nothing else you paid comes back.

Reserve.fieldHealth: How much Health is left. Type a number to change it.
Reserve.fieldSanity: How much Sanity is left. Type a number to change it.

Murder.openingReask: Ask for the opening roll again
Murder.openingReaskSent: The opening roll was offered again: to the victim of a trap, otherwise to the killer.
Murder.openingReaskWait: The opening roll was offered a moment ago. Wait a few seconds before asking again.
Murder.victimNoticedNext: The victim noticed the trap. Nothing moves on by itself: they may use their Free Move if they still have it, and the incident stays open until you end it from the tracker.
Murder.openIntro: An incident opens on one roll, then runs in turns. In a direct murder the killer rolls; in a trap, the victim.
Murder.indirect: A trap (the victim alone, losing double)
Murder.indirectCost: A trap is built as projects. Plan about {low}-{high} progress in total, roughly {fewest} to {actions}.
Murder.needOne: A murder needs at least one living student, who can hold both seats.
Murder.openSelfNote: The same student as killer and victim makes this a death by their own hand, and the trap box is cleared and locked. There is no fight: the opening roll decides whether they go through with it, and if they do, the incident goes straight to the clean-up.
Murder.killerNotAlive: {name} was named as the killer but is not among the living, so the Killer list shows someone else. Choose the killer.
Murder.roomsDiffer: {killer} is in {killerRoom}, {victim} in {victimRoom}. Bring them together, or open it anyway.
Murder.opened: {killer} is moving on {victim}. The opening roll has gone to {roller}.
Murder.openedSelf: {name} means to take their own life. The opening roll has gone to them.
Murder.openedSelfNote: There is no fight to run. If the roll succeeds, the incident goes straight to the clean-up, where they arrange the scene before dying; if it fails, it ends and nobody dies. They stay alive until you close the incident.
Murder.selfWentThrough: You went through with it. There is no fight. The clean-up is open on your sheet: while you are alive, you can see and clean your own Remnants.
Murder.resolutionNoteSelf: The clean-up begins. They can see and clean their own Remnants while still alive; the death is recorded when you close the incident.
Murder.afterSelf: By their own hand: nobody else was in the room, and the class has only the scene to go on.
Murder.afterIntroSelf: {name}, by their own hand. The incident is closed; below is what follows from it, and nothing here asks for an answer.
Murder.dayNote: It is not night, so night does not change the opening roll.

keyCount.one: This case will leave {n} Key Remnant.
keyCount.other: This case will leave {n} Key Remnants.

Murder.trackerCastGone: A character this incident names no longer exists ({who}). Nothing can move it on: press End the murder.
Murder.ranOut: {name} has no Health and no Sanity left, and is dead. The incident ends without a Finishing Blow, so no clean-up attempt is free.
Murder.rerollLost: A Reroll of a crisis action could not be carried out: its record was missing, or the incident closed or moved on first. The first roll stands and the Hope is returned. If the incident closed meanwhile, check that action's Remnant and the sheets by hand.
Murder.passTooSoon: The turn was passed a moment ago. Press Pass the turn again to pass the next one.
Murder.endConfirm: Stop tracking this murder? Lost Health and Sanity, items, and Remnants stay as they are.
Murder.afterIntro: {killer} against {victim}. The incident is closed; below is what follows from it.
Murder.afterNoRoom: The victim's token is outside every room. Put it where the body is before announcing it.
Murder.afterAutopsy: The autopsy Truth Bullet has not been issued.
Murder.afterDirect: A direct murder: whoever was in the room saw it happen.
Murder.afterIndirect: A trap: nobody saw it, and setting it left Remnants of its own.
Murder.escapeIntro: {victim} and {third} got away from {killer}. Nobody died: there is no body to announce, no autopsy to issue, and no Class Trial to hold.
Murder.escapeRoom: It happened in {room}, and what the fight left behind is still there.
Murder.escapeNoRoom: No room is recorded for this incident, so place whatever it left behind by hand.
Murder.escapeWitness: {victim} and {third} both saw who it was. What they do with that is the table's business.
Murder.escapeKiller: {killer} is not Blackened. Nothing has changed for them except that two people know.
Murder.afterSurvived: {victim} lived through the fight with {killer}. Nobody died and nobody is Blackened: there is no body to announce, no autopsy to issue, and no Class Trial to hold. What the fight left behind is still where it fell.
Murder.afterInterrupted: The incident was interrupted before anything was decided. Nobody died and nobody is Blackened: there is no body and no autopsy. What the fight left behind is still where it fell.
Murder.closedVictimYou: The incident is over. You can act again.
Murder.useItemGone: You no longer carry that item.
Murder.useItemFumbled: The item stays in their pocket, and somebody saw them reaching for it.
Murder.useItemAsked: The GM decides if it works. Until then the item is not used up.
Murder.actionBlocked: The killer has blocked this action for now.
Murder.actionHindered: The killer made this harder: you roll at disadvantage.
Murder.nothingLeftToSpend: You have no Sanity or Health left to spend.
Murder.advantageNext: Advantage on the next attempt at this action.
Murder.noKillerLeft: Every killer in this incident is dead. The victim takes every turn until you close the incident.
Murder.killerChooses: Critical - the killer chooses where both points come off: Health or Sanity.

hinderedActions.one: The victim rolls {actions} at disadvantage for {turns} turn of their own.
hinderedActions.other: The victim rolls {actions} at disadvantage for {turns} turns of their own.

blockedActions.one: The victim cannot use {actions} for {turns} turn of their own.
blockedActions.other: The victim cannot use {actions} for {turns} turns of their own.

Murder.rolesSwapped: The roles are reversed: the former killer is now the victim and loses Sanity each turn, then Health once Sanity runs out. The turn passes to the new killer, and unlocked and spent actions and hindrances start over.
Murder.victimDead: The victim is dead. The killer is Blackened.
Murder.resolutionNote: The clean-up begins. The killer now sees the Remnants on the map and can clean them up, except Reinforced ones, which stay. The Murder Weapon that was swung breaks when the incident closes.
Murder.thirdIntro: You get one choice: get the victim out with you, take a side, or turn away.
Murder.actionSpent: You have already taken that one this incident.
Murder.actionDenied: That action is not open to you now.
Murder.drainStopped: The bleeding stops: the victim no longer loses Sanity or Health each turn. The other side's blows still do damage.
Murder.indirectBegins: The trap closes. The incident begins with the victim alone: they lose 2 a turn, Sanity first, then Health, and roll every crisis roll with advantage.
Murder.tierZeroIntro: {actor} swings “{item}”, a Tier 0 object. Used creatively, it may count as Tier 1 or 2: rate this use.
Murder.tierZeroNote: Tier 0 takes 1 Health, Tier 1 takes 2, and Tier 2 takes 2, or 3 on a critical. Closing the window leaves it at Tier 0.
Murder.improvised: The killer snatches a weapon out of the struggle: “{item}” (Tier {tier}).
Murder.improvisedNote: Grabbed mid-incident. A Murder Weapon like any other.
Murder.cannotLeave: You cannot leave during an incident. Only a crisis action gets you out: Survive, Escape Together, a Finishing Blow, or, if you only walked in on it, Averted Eyes.
Murder.oneAtATime: An incident is already running. End it before you open another.
Murder.crisisPrompt: What are you doing about it?
Murder.crisisBrief: One action a turn. A row that is shut says why.
Murder.nothingToDo: There is nothing left for you to do this round.
Murder.actionsLocked: During an incident you act through {tile}. Hope Calls still work.
Murder.thirdJoined: {name} throws in with the killer and stays in the incident.
Murder.thirdLeft: {name} turns away and leaves. They take no part in this.
Murder.thirdEscapedAlone: {name} gets out alone and leaves the incident. The victim stays.
Murder.openingYours: This opening roll is yours, and it cannot be skipped. If you close the window, it opens again, and after a few refusals the GMs are told.
Murder.openingRequired: This roll cannot be skipped. Roll it.
Murder.openingDeclined: {name} did not make the opening roll, and it cannot be skipped. Press Ask for the opening roll again on the Incident tracker, or end the incident.
Murder.openingRemnantNote: {name} sensed the attempt ({band}). Something of the struggle was left to notice.

leftRemnants.one: This leaves a Remnant the killer cannot wipe.
leftRemnants.other: This leaves {n} Remnants the killer cannot wipe.

keyRemnantsStale.one: The roles reversed, so the Key Remnant was planned around a killer who is now the victim. Write a new one before the Investigation; the opening roll set the count at {n}, and it stays.
keyRemnantsStale.other: The roles reversed, so the {n} Key Remnants were planned around a killer who is now the victim. Write {n} new ones before the Investigation; the opening roll set the count, and it stays.

Murder.nightNoteDirect: It is night: the killer's opening roll has advantage.
Murder.nightNoteNone: It is night, but night does not change this opening roll.
Murder.nightNoteIndirect: It is night: the victim's opening roll has disadvantage.
Murder.betrayalNote: {third} walked in on this and is still standing, and may turn on {killer} until the day ends. Outside an Eclipse it is the one killing that needs no declaration in advance; during one it is declared and opens when the Eclipse ends.
Murder.betrayalIntro: {third} turns on {killer}. This opens a second murder, with {third} as the killer and {killer} as the victim, from a new opening roll.
Murder.betrayalRule: Two bodies in one day give the Class Trial two killings to untangle, and the Blackened of the first is not automatically the Blackened of the second. You can decide until the day ends.
Murder.betrayalConfirmEclipse: During an Eclipse the betrayal is declared now and opens when the Eclipse ends. It costs an action, which stays spent even if the betrayal cannot open then.
Murder.betrayalParked: Your betrayal is declared. It opens when the Eclipse ends.
Murder.betrayalAnnounce: The betrayal opens a second incident on {killer}.
Murder.betrayalRefused: The betrayal could not open: {why}. It stays on offer until the day ends.

betrayalWhy.spent: it is no longer on offer
betrayalWhy.failed: the new incident did not start
betrayalWhy.trial: a Class Trial is in session
betrayalWhy.dead: one of the two is no longer alive

Murder.victimUnderAttackBy: {killer} is moving on you. The incident has begun, and the first turn is yours: press Fight Back under Actions on your character sheet.
Murder.victimSomeoneMoves: Someone is moving on you. The incident has begun, and the first turn is yours: press Fight Back under Actions on your character sheet.
Murder.victimTrapSprung: The trap closes. You did not see it in time. The incident has begun, and the first turn is yours: press Fight Back under Actions on your character sheet.
Murder.offTurn: It is their turn. Your crisis actions open when it comes back to you.
Murder.breakdownDisadvantage: You are in Breakdown, so this roll is at disadvantage until some Sanity comes back.
Murder.gmPicksTrait: Rolls {traits}: you propose one below, and the GM approves or changes it.
Murder.youPickTrait: Rolls {traits}: with Resolve armed, you pick one in the roll window.
Murder.criticalChoiceIntro: The blow lands exactly where you wanted it. Choose where both points go: all to their Health or all to their Sanity. Closing the window picks Health.
Murder.ranOutTwoKillers: {victim} is out of Health and Sanity, and {killers} are both in this.
Murder.ranOutTwoKillersNote: End it now and the incident moves to the clean-up. Or let the turns go on, so no one loses a turn they were owed, and end it from the tracker later.
Murder.crowded: {name} walked in after {third}. With four people in the room, the incident is canceled.
Murder.crowdedNote: Nobody dies. What the fight already did stands: the Health and Sanity lost, and the Remnants it left.
Murder.freeResolution: This turn the victim can take Survive or Role Reversal, whichever is open, with no roll, and it works.
Murder.castMissingHere: This browser lacks the incident's cast and cannot work out the turn. Press Enter the cast by hand in the health check, or let a GM who holds it act.
Murder.castNotArrived: The other GMs' copies of the incident's cast have not reached this browser yet. Try again in a moment.
Murder.deniedByIncident: The incident has taken this one away from you.

Investigation.finalAskBody: A room is picked for the Final Truth Remnant, but the window was closed without Save. Place it now?
Investigation.plannedRoomGone: The planned room “{room}” is not on this scene. Pick a room.
Investigation.neverOnePerson: A trace never names anyone: a Key Remnant narrows it to at most half the cast, any other to 2-4.

plannerIntro.one: {n} clue for chapter {chapter}. Together they should narrow the suspects to {min}-{max} people.
plannerIntro.other: {n} clues for chapter {chapter}. Together they should narrow the suspects to {min}-{max} people.

Investigation.placedMeanwhile: Another GM placed this row's Key Remnant while the window was open, so nothing more was placed.
Investigation.tokenGone: Its Remnant is gone from the map
Investigation.keyRetyped: Its Remnant is no longer a Key Remnant

keyOffPlan.one: One more found Key Remnant is not on the plan and counts toward the threshold of {bar}: {names}.
keyOffPlan.other: {n} more found Key Remnants are not on the plan and count toward the threshold of {bar}: {names}.

Investigation.deleteTraceAsk: Delete the Remnant “{name}”? Its token goes from the map and its row from the case.

tooThin.one: Only {found} Key Remnant has been found. The minimum is {min} - below that the trial has no honest answer. Point the players at what is left, or let it stand and pay for it at the vote.
tooThin.other: Only {found} Key Remnants have been found. The minimum is {min} - below that the trial has no honest answer. Point the players at what is left, or let it stand and pay for it at the vote.

Investigation.tooThinNone: No Key Remnant has been found yet. The minimum is {min} - below that the trial has no honest answer. Point the players at what is left, or let it stand and pay for it at the vote.
Investigation.breakdownTooltip: What each Truth Bullet really is, by the GMs' answer key - not what its holder was shown.
Investigation.newTraceIntro: It lands at a random spot in the room; move the token if the spot matters.
Investigation.newTraceTied: Part of this murder (survives the chapter-end sweep)
Investigation.newTraceNote: The name and the description are what a student reads when they find it; what analysis reveals waits for their Analyze. Your note stays yours.
Investigation.newTraceBadType: That is not a kind of Remnant this module knows.
Investigation.newTraceUnfindable: Nothing can find a Remnant of that kind at that difficulty - Observe has no number for it.
Investigation.noRooms: This scene has no rooms on it yet, so there is nowhere to put a Remnant. Draw the regions first - Room setup explains how.
Investigation.createNote: Place puts a row's Key Remnant on the map at once, in the room you pick: reinforced, tied to the crime, somewhere inside the room, with the words typed on its row. A row already on the map has no Place button.
Investigation.keyDcNote: A Key Remnant is the easiest thing in a room to notice, and how easy depends on where you put it, not on the scale above: {list}. Ordinary evidence in the same band is three to six harder. The scale is how much a clue gives away.
Investigation.keyLimitLine: {used} of {limit} used this chapter - the minimum is {min}.
Investigation.keyLimitOverride: Create more than the opening roll allows

savedOver.one: One field had changed elsewhere while this window was open, and was not saved: {list}. Open Investigation again to see what it holds now; type yours again if it should stand.
savedOver.other: {n} fields had changed elsewhere while this window was open, and were not saved: {list}. Open Investigation again to see what they hold now; type yours again if they should stand.

Investigation.saveStopped: The Save stopped part-way: {error}. What it wrote before that stands and the rest was not saved; Investigation is open again on what the world holds now - type the rest again.

createHereIntro.one: They named a point of interest and you have decided there is something there. This puts it on the map, and can hang it on the {n} clue you planned.
createHereIntro.other: They named a point of interest and you have decided there is something there. This puts it on the map, and can hang it on one of the {n} clues you planned.

unfoundKeys.one: The investigation turned up {found} of {bar} Key Remnants - one short. {despair} Despair to each pool: {who}.
unfoundKeys.other: The investigation turned up {found} of {bar} Key Remnants - {n} short. {despair} Despair to each pool: {who}.

Investigation.keyPublicNote: Name and Player description are what a finder holds the moment they pick it up; What analysis reveals waits for their Analyze. The same three fields the Remnants tab edits. Your note stays yours.

leftoverKeys.one: {n} Key Remnant from an earlier chapter is still on the map. This chapter's plan cannot see it; clear it at the end of a chapter or attach it here.
leftoverKeys.other: {n} Key Remnants from an earlier chapter are still on the map. This chapter's plan cannot see them; clear them at the end of a chapter or attach them here.

Investigation.chargeTooLate: The clock has already moved to chapter {now}, and the last case was chapter {was}'s: this chapter has no case of its own to count unfound Key Remnants against, so nothing was charged.

Vault.handsFull: Your hands are full: what you found in the stash stays where it was.
Vault.stowTooltip: Put this in your stash (you must be in the room)
Vault.takeTooltip: Take this back out (you must be in the room)
Vault.notHere: Your stash is in {room} - stand there to reach it.
Vault.noStashOnScene: You have no stash on this scene.
Vault.handFirst: “{item}” cannot be held ready, and only one {group} may be stowed. Take a working one in hand first.
Vault.noBullets: Truth Bullets are what you know, not things in a stash.
Vault.full: {room} is full. A stash holds {limit} things - take something out before putting something in.
Vault.overflowed: Your hands were full, so “{item}” went into your stash. Your {category} limit is unchanged.
Vault.rifledAgain: You have already been through {who}'s stash this time of day. Try it again at the next time of day.
Vault.noticed: Something has been moved in your stash, and something is missing from it. You have no idea whose hands have been in it, or when.
Vault.gmPending: {thief} took something from the stash of {owner} in {room} while {owner} was elsewhere. {owner} will be told somebody has been in it on next entering that room - never who or when.
Vault.gmWatched: {thief} took something from the stash of {owner} in {room} while {owner} stood there. {owner} saw it, so no notice waits.
Vault.gmTold: {owner} entered {room} and was told somebody has been in their stash. It covers the reaches of: {names}.
Vault.stashesIntro: Who has a stash in which room. Click a cell to change it. A bedroom's owner has a stash there from the start; you can take it away here.
Vault.stashesNote: Anyone in the room can go through an open stash and take one thing from it, once a time of day. A hidden one must be found first, with Analyze's Find Stash (16+), and is open to its finder from then on. A stash in somebody else's room does NOT come with a key to it.
Vault.stashCycle: Click to cycle: none / open / hidden

stashNotEmpty.one: {name} has one thing in the stash in {room} - take it out before removing it.
stashNotEmpty.other: {name} has {n} things in the stash in {room} - take them out before removing it.

Vault.manageNote: A good place gives advantage when searching for that category, a bad one disadvantage. A room with no table draws from the global pool.
Vault.roomRatio: {rooms}, {per} rooms per student. Living students: {living}; this season wants {want} ({target} each).

roomCensusUndecided.one: Not counted yet: {n} region nobody has decided, ticked as a suggestion - Apply makes it a room.
roomCensusUndecided.other: Not counted yet: {n} regions nobody has decided, ticked as suggestions - Apply makes them rooms.

Vault.searchIntro: What a Search draws in each room, how many tokens it has, and what is worth looking for there.
Vault.placeColumn: Good or bad place to look for
Vault.placeCycle: Click to cycle: neither / good place / bad place
Vault.noRooms: This scene has no room regions yet.
Vault.noneSet: No bedrooms have been assigned yet.
Vault.twoRooms: {name} cannot have two bedrooms ({a} and {b}). Pick one.
Vault.applyLine: Apply saves every tab at once. Secret passages, the Search Token buttons and room actions work at once, without Apply.
Vault.roomsIntro: Which regions are rooms, whose bedroom each is, and which are not counted as private. One student, one bedroom.
Vault.notSharedLine: “No privacy”: corridors, stairs and places where nobody talks privately. It changes only the room count.
Vault.doorsLine: Which doors are locked now, and which at the start of a season.
Vault.neighboursLine: “Neighbours”: list the rooms this one has doors to, separated by commas; it works both ways. Left blank, the walls decide (grey names).
Vault.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. Long tables, a serving hatch, and a smell of bleach nobody can place.
Vault.descriptionIntro: What each room looks like. Whoever stands in it sees the text and picture on their room tile.
Vault.descriptionNote: Plain text, shown as typed; an empty line starts a new paragraph. Pictures come only from this game's files, or on The Forge from your Assets Library. Every browser holds the descriptions and pictures of all rooms, so keep a room's secrets in its stashes and traces.
Vault.imageRefused: {room}: the picture was not saved. Pick a jpg, png, webp, or avif from this game's files, or on The Forge from your Assets Library.
Vault.fogIntro: Which rooms each character has found on this scene. Found rooms show through a light veil, not fog.
Vault.fogUncovered: {pct}% of this scene's surface belongs to no room region at all - it will show as permanent fog rather than a wall gap, which usually means a room still needs drawing.
Vault.fogNote: Discover all / Hide all tick or clear every checkbox above for every character at once. Nothing changes until you press Apply. The individual checkboxes are for one room, one character.
Vault.inspectNote: Take things out from Give / take items - a stashed item is an ordinary item on its owner's sheet.
Vault.rifleIntro: Stashes you can reach in {room}: {who}. Take one thing from each, once each time of day.
Vault.rifleNote: Free. A hidden stash you have not found has to be found first, with Analyze's Find Stash.
Vault.noOpenStashHere: There is no open stash in this room.
Vault.openStashNote: You can take one thing from each stash listed here, once each time of day.
Vault.keyDescription: Opens the door to {room}, which belongs to {owner}. Share a copy to let somebody else in.
Vault.keyShared: {who} gave you a copy of the key to {room}.
Vault.keyGave: {who} now has a copy of your key to {room}.
Vault.keyMissing: The door to {room} is locked. You do not have that key.
Vault.giveKeyNote: A copy - the owner keeps theirs. Only rooms that belong to somebody are listed: a room with no owner has no door to unlock.
Vault.keyDuplicatesTaken: {actor} held more than one key to {room}: one is kept, and the extra copies were taken.
Vault.keyTakenGm: {actor} no longer holds the key to {room}: the room is not theirs any more.
Vault.keyTakenBack: Your key to {room} was taken back: the room is not yours any more.
Vault.keyCopiesTakenGm: Copies of the key to {room} went with the room: taken from {holders}.
Vault.keyCopyTakenBack: Your copy of the key to {room} was taken back: the room changed hands.
Vault.noKeysToGive: No keys left to hand over - this character already holds one for every bedroom that has an owner.
Vault.hasEveryKey: {name} already holds a key to every bedroom that has an owner.
Vault.onlyOwnBedroom: The only bedroom with an owner is {name}'s own. There is no key to give.
Vault.noKeysToTake: {actor} holds no key to anybody else's room.
Vault.brokenHint: A lock forced open (Force the Door, a breach). While ticked the door opens for everyone; untick it to repair the lock.
Vault.lockedAtStartHint: Whether this door is locked when a season begins. A season reset puts every door back to this.
Vault.isRoomHint: Whether this region is a room. A region with a Teleport or level-change behaviour, or one a player drew, cannot be one.
Vault.notSharedHint: Leave this region out of the rooms-per-player count. Changes no rule.
Vault.neighboursHint: The rooms this one has a door to, separated by commas. Blank: its walls decide (the greyed names).
Vault.neighboursNote: “Neighbours” is where a door overrules the map: list the rooms this one opens into, separated by commas. Two rooms are connected when either lists the other, both ways. A room with a list is connected to nothing else, and a room beside it cannot walk in unless one of the two lists the other. Left blank, a room's neighbours are the rooms without a list whose walls share an edge with its own (a corner is not enough), and every room that lists it. A room the lists and the walls leave with no neighbour has no door out. A room that has no list, is in no list and touches no other room, not even at a corner, is not checked: a crossing from it may go to any room.
Vault.neighboursUnknown: {room}: no room on this scene is named {names}. Kept in its Neighbours, where it connects nothing.
Vault.imageLarge: This picture is large and slow to load for every player: {size}.
Vault.imageBroken: This picture does not load - pick the file again.

Chapter.keepBullets: Keep their Truth Bullets (not a killing-game death)
Chapter.deathNote: Their Truth Bullets are destroyed, carried and stashed alike, and that cannot be undone. Everything else stays on the body to be found, and the dead move none of it. The dead stop counting as being in the room: no witnessing, no handovers, no murder blocked.
Chapter.vaultPending: A stash is still their own sheet, so stashed bullets are in the count above and everything else they put away stays there to be found.
Chapter.stageSixTitle: That was the victim of the incident
Chapter.stageSixIntro: {victim} is the victim of the incident {killer} is in, and the incident is still running.
Chapter.stageSixWhat: Moving it to Stage 6 lets {killer} see the Remnants they left and spend Sanity trying to erase them. The incident stays open until you close it, so nothing is announced yet.
Chapter.revived: {name} is no longer marked dead. The Truth Bullets that died with them do not come back.
Chapter.deadPanelNote: The dead take no actions and spend no Hope. Brought back as a Monocub, this panel holds Confusion and the Monocub's other tiles.
Chapter.deadCannotAct: {name} is dead and cannot take actions.
Chapter.keepSecretUntilFound: Keep it the GMs' until the body is found: no flag, no marker, and their Truth Bullets stay until then
Chapter.keptUntilFound: Kept by the GMs until the body is found or you make it known in the Players window. The table sees nothing yet: no flag, no marker, and their Truth Bullets are still on the sheet.
Chapter.nobodyFoundYou: Nobody has found your body yet.
Chapter.youFoundBody: In {room} you find the body of {name}. Nobody else has seen it yet, and nothing is announced.
Chapter.youFoundBodyWith: In {room} you find the body of {name}. You are not the only one here, and nothing is announced until the GM says so.
Chapter.pendingBody: {names} found the body of {name} in {room}. Announce the discovery now?
Chapter.pendingNote: Announce brings everyone to the room and plays the discovery sound to the whole table. Not yet keeps it waiting: you can announce it later with Body found in the Investigation window.

deathsStillSecret.one: {n} death nobody has found is still the GMs' alone. Until you make it known in the Players window, this trial treats that student as living - they vote and level up with the class - and does not ask for their killer, who counts as a Blackened only for a death the table knows.
deathsStillSecret.other: {n} deaths nobody has found are still the GMs' alone. Until you make them known in the Players window, this trial treats those students as living - they vote and level up with the class - and does not ask for their killers, who count as Blackened only for a death the table knows.

Chapter.bodyAnnouncedAlready: {name}'s body was already announced in this chapter, so nothing was announced again. To announce another body in that room, leave the body unnamed.
Chapter.bodyPrimaryOnly: Only the primary GM, {name}, can announce a body. Ask {name}, or announce it when you are the only GM connected.
Chapter.bodyNotPublished: {name}'s death could not be made known to the table, so the discovery does not name them and the death is still the GMs' alone. Make it known in the Players window.
Chapter.noRooms: This scene has no room regions to gather anyone into.
Chapter.bodyNote: Everyone is called to the room. The phase does not change until you start the Investigation.
Chapter.bodyNoteLater: Everyone is called to the room. The phase does not change.
Chapter.bodyNoteTraces: Then you are asked which Remnants left while somebody gathered tools belong to this murder.
Chapter.bodyFound: A body has been found in {room}.
Chapter.bodyCalled: Everyone is gathered in the room with the body. The GM will start the Investigation.

promoted.one: {n} Remnant now counts as evidence of this murder.
promoted.other: {n} Remnants now count as evidence of this murder.

Chapter.promoteIntro: These Prep Remnants were left while somebody gathered tools. Most mean nothing. Tick the ones that belong to this killing.
Chapter.promoteNote: Ticked Remnants stop being doubtful: they count as evidence tied to the crime, and a Faint clear will not take them. Leave the rest and they stay Faint.
Chapter.endIntro: Chapter {chapter} is wrapping up. Tick what should happen.
Chapter.optReveal: Reveal what the Truth Bullets really are, with their readings ({n} to reveal)
Chapter.revealKeeps: Faint Truth Bullets stay hidden, but every Final, Faint or not, shows its kind; both stay, still to be analysed.
Chapter.lastChapter: Chapter {n} is the last of a season. Press Reset the season in Season setup (GM panel, Between sessions) rather than moving on to chapter {next}.
Chapter.optNextMorning: Open the next chapter on the morning of day {day}, with actions and search tokens refilled
Chapter.moved: The clock now reads chapter {chapter}, session {session}.

typeless.one: 1 Truth Bullet not analysed has no real type recorded, so revealing cannot touch it - {who} holds it. Take it, and give one with its type from Give / take items.
typeless.other: {n} Truth Bullets not analysed have no real type recorded, so revealing cannot touch them - held by {who}. Take them, and give ones with their types from Give / take items.

Chapter.optSweep: Collect the Truth Bullets ({n} would go, Faint and Final stay)
Chapter.optFaint: Clear the Faint Remnants ({n} would go)
Chapter.optKeys: Take this chapter's Key Remnants off the map ({n})

doneKeys.one: Took {n} Key Remnant off the map.
doneKeys.other: Took {n} Key Remnants off the map.

Chapter.optEndTrial: Close the trial and return everyone to Daily Life
Chapter.finalTruthMissing: No Final Truth Remnant was placed this chapter. One a chapter points at the Mastermind: place it from The case > Investigation, on the Final Truth Remnants tab.
Chapter.doneEndTrial: Closed the trial; the campaign is back in Daily Life.
Chapter.doneNextMorning: The next chapter opens on the morning of day {day}, with actions and Search Tokens refilled.
Chapter.doneInvestigationOver: The Investigation is over; the campaign is back in Daily Life.
Chapter.endTwice: This End of chapter window was opened on chapter {chapter}, session {session}, day {day}, and the clock's chapter, session, or day has moved since - by another End of chapter, by Edit campaign, or by the time of day turning into a new day. Nothing was done: open End of chapter again to choose against the clock as it stands now.
Chapter.endPhaseMoved: This End of chapter window was opened in {opened}, and the clock has read {now} since - the phase changed after the window was drawn, so what it offered to close is not what is sitting now. Nothing was done: open End of chapter again to choose against the clock as it stands now.
Chapter.endPrimaryOnly: Only the primary GM, {name}, can end the chapter. Ask {name}, or end it when you are the only GM connected.
Chapter.endFailed: The end of the chapter stopped at: {steps}. Finish the chapter's end does the rest.
Chapter.endStopped: The phase changed from {opened} to {now} while the chapter was ending, so these did not run: {steps}. Back in {opened}, Finish the chapter's end does the rest; Drop the rest leaves them undone.
Chapter.endStands: The last end of the chapter stopped at: {steps}.
Chapter.notStopped: No end of the chapter waits to be finished.
Chapter.finishPhaseMoved: The end of the chapter stopped in {opened}, and the clock reads {now}. Back in {opened}, Finish the chapter's end does the rest; Drop the rest leaves it undone.
Chapter.endStoppedPrimary: The end of the chapter stopped: this browser is no longer the primary GM's - {name} is - so these did not run: {steps}. What ran stays done; on {name}'s browser, Finish the chapter's end does the rest.
Chapter.endNotRecorded: The end of the chapter could not write down how far it has got ({error}). Nothing was done.

step.keys: taking the Key Remnants off the map

TrialScene.castUnavailable: The trial opened and nobody in the trial hall was shown: the GMs' choice of its tokens had not reached this client yet. Show them by hand on the hall's scene.
TrialScene.duplicateToken: More than one token in the trial hall stands for the same character, and only the first was shown. Kept hidden: {names}.
TrialScene.playerTokenCreated: {user} made a token in the trial hall: {name}. It is hidden - showing the hall's tokens is the GM's - and stays where it is; the next trial treats it as any token of the hall.
TrialScene.playerTokenDeleted: {user} deleted a token from the trial hall: {name}. If the module made it, it makes it again the next time the trial opens; if a GM placed it, put it back by hand if the trial needs it.
TrialScene.hiddenPutBack: {user} changed whether {name} is hidden in the trial hall. Showing and hiding the hall's tokens is the GM's, so it was put back as the GMs left it.
TrialScene.noSchool: The Class Trial ended, but no school scene is linked and the scene the trial opened from is gone, so the table stays in the trial hall and its tokens stay as they are. Activate a scene by hand.

notMoved.one: {n} living student could not be moved and stays where they stood: {names}. Move them by hand.
notMoved.other: {n} living students could not be moved and stay where they stood: {names}. Move them by hand.

carryUnfinished.one: {n} student carried out of the Class Trial stands twice - the copy and the token it was made from, which was not deleted: {names}. Delete the one you do not want.
carryUnfinished.other: {n} students carried out of the Class Trial stand twice - each a copy and the token it was made from, which was not deleted: {names}. Delete the ones you do not want.

hiddenHere.one: {n} living student's token in the room is hidden, and a shown token of theirs stays on another scene: {names}.
hiddenHere.other: {n} living students' tokens in the room are hidden, and shown tokens of theirs stay on other scenes: {names}.

tokensStay.one: {n} living student in the room still has a token on another scene, left where it stood: {names}.
tokensStay.other: {n} living students in the room still have a token on another scene, left where it stood: {names}.

TrialScene.scenesIntro: Link the school and the trial hall (a scene of its own) once a season. When the Class Trial opens, everyone goes to the hall and the students ticked below get tokens there. Nothing deletes your tokens in the hall.

hallRoom.legend: The trial hall on the room tile
hallRoom.hint: Everybody sees these on the room tile during the Class Trial. Write nothing secret here.
hallRoom.name: Name

zones.zonesNone: The trial hall has no zones. Straw Poll, Logic Dive and Scrum Debate need Zone A and Zone B: pick two regions of the hall above.
zones.zoneMissing: Only one zone is picked, or a zone's region is gone. Pick both Zone A and Zone B.
zones.zonesSame: Zone A and Zone B are the same region. Pick two different regions.
zones.zonesOverlap: Zone A and Zone B overlap. A token whose centre stands in both is counted on neither side.

zones.zonesUnchecked: This hall has no grid, and whether the zones cover it could not be checked in time.

TrialScene.reveal: Ticked: a token in the hall, and back to the chosen room after the trial. Unticked: does not appear (a test student, say).
TrialScene.noCast: The world has no student or Monokuma yet.
TrialScene.sameScene: The school and the trial hall are the same scene. Pick two different scenes - Apply waits until then.
TrialScene.hallInTrial: A Class Trial is running in the linked trial hall. End the trial before you link another hall or unlink this one - Apply waits until then.
TrialScene.hallFirstInTrial: A Class Trial is running without a trial hall. Link one after the trial ends - Apply waits until then.
TrialScene.noSchoolLinked: With no school linked, ending the trial goes back to the scene before it.
TrialScene.hallHasRooms: This scene has regions marked as rooms: {names}. In the trial hall they are not rooms - is this the school's map? Regions not marked as rooms are fine here.
TrialScene.duplicateInHall: More than one token in the hall stands for the same character, and a trial shows only the first. The others: {names}.

TrialScene.hallDarkLine: The trial hall still has Foundry's token vision on, its global light off or its exploration fog on. For everyone to see the whole hall, tick "Prepare the hall on Save" in Season setup and press Save.
TrialScene.noWayBackLine: No school is linked and the scene the trial opened from is gone, so the table stays in the trial hall. Link a school in Season setup.
TrialScene.noWayBack: No school is linked and the scene the trial opened from is gone, so the table stays in the trial hall. Link a school in Room setup's Scenes tab.
TrialScene.phaseSwitchesScene: It also takes everyone to the trial hall, {hall}, and places the tokens of the students chosen for it.

notPlaced.other: The trial hall has no token for {n} of the trial's cast, so the trial cannot show them: {names}. The module makes none for Monokuma, and one it could not make is in the console - place one for each on the hall's scene by hand.

TrialScene.handPlaced: {names}: no token in the trial hall, and the module makes none for Monokuma - place one by hand if the trial needs it.

Trial.commentPlaceholder: e.g. This is why the timeline does not work.

Trial.notInTrial: Evidence is presented in a Class Trial. Outside one, share a copy instead.

logSummary.other: {total} presented this chapter, {objections} of them as an Objection that took the floor.

Trial.objectionRefunded: Your Objection did not take the floor: {why} What you paid ({what}) was given back, and the card is marked as refused.

Trial.objectionNotYours: That Objection was posted by somebody who does not own {name}, so the floor did not move.
Trial.objectionNoItem: That Objection named no evidence, so the floor did not move.
Trial.deadCannotPresent: {name} is dead, and the dead neither present evidence nor object.
Trial.presentByButton: Evidence is presented with Present on your sheet, and the GM's browser posts its card. That card was not posted that way, so nobody was shown it.
Trial.presentPair: Only {a} and {b} can present right now.
Trial.presentWithAnalysis: Show it with my Analyze result
Trial.presentWithoutNote: Unticked, the card and everybody's copy show it as never analysed: no reading, no type it turned out to be.
Trial.presentCopy: {who} presented {name}. A copy, as it was shown, is now on your sheet.
Trial.logEmpty: Nothing has been presented this chapter yet.
Trial.objectionNobody: There is nobody else left to object to.

objectionWarning.one: Once your Truth Bullet is on the table, the debate is yours: {objection} second in which only you may speak.
objectionWarning.other: Once your Truth Bullet is on the table, the debate is yours: {objection} seconds in which only you may speak.

objectionWarningRebuttal.one: Then {rebuttal} second of rebuttal with the one you objected to.
objectionWarningRebuttal.other: Then {rebuttal} seconds of rebuttal with the one you objected to.

Trial.actionsLocked: The Class Trial is in session. Only Analyze and an Objection are open - and your Hope Calls.
Trial.moveLocked: The Class Trial is in session. Nobody leaves the courtroom until it ends.
Trial.callsLocked: The Class Trial is in session. Despair Calls wait for it to end.
Trial.objectionNoFloor: The debate is not open, so there is nothing to interrupt. Show the evidence instead.
Trial.objectionNotParticipant: An Objection can only be aimed at somebody taking part in the trial.

Trial.objectionNoGm: No GM is connected, so nobody can hand over the floor. Put the evidence on the table instead.
Trial.objectionOutside: Objection only in a Class Trial.

Trial.objectionByButton: An Objection is raised with OBJECTION! on the HUD, not from the sheet. Press it, then choose your Truth Bullet.
Trial.objectionWithdrawn: withdrawn - no Truth Bullet was presented
Trial.objectionPickIntro: Your Objection is aimed at {target}. Choose the Truth Bullet that proves it.

objectionPickCount.other: {seconds} s left to choose. When they run out the Objection is withdrawn, and what you paid is not given back.

Trial.objectionAtLast: OBJECTION! at {target}, the last to speak.

Trial.objectionNoRoom: The GM is not connected to a voice channel, so name whom you contradict.

Handover.stashed: {name} is in a stash, not in your hands. Take it out first.

Handover.changedMidway: “{name}” changed on {from}'s sheet while it was on its way to {to} - used, broken, or gone. Nothing changed hands.
Handover.changedMidwayKept: “{name}” changed on {from}'s sheet while it was on its way to {to} - used, broken, or gone - and the copy could not be taken back. There is one too many now - remove it from {to}'s sheet.

gaveOne.one: You hand {who} one {name}. You still have one.
gaveOne.other: You hand {who} one {name}. You still have {left}.

Handover.receivedBulletFrom: {who} showed you {name}, and you have written down a copy.
Handover.answerKeyMissing: {name} cannot be handed over now: the GM's record of what it really is is missing. The GM can bring it back from a backup (GM panel, Diagnostics, The case: Restore from a file).

Observe.projectFoundDone: The secret project you found is finished: {name}.
Observe.anythingTitle: Observe - a question for the GM
Observe.requestPlaceholder: e.g. something to do with the body
Observe.requestSkipped: Nothing named - read as looking around.
Observe.sent: The GM is judging your Observe and will send you the result.
Observe.projectFoundTitle: Something here is not what it looks like
Observe.projectFound: Under the surface of the room, somebody has been building: {name}. You know about it now. Its progress shows as it was on your last visit, and updates when you come back here.
Observe.critIdentified: You found it, and you know what kind of Remnant it is.
Observe.whichRemnant: Which Remnant are they closest to?
Observe.pickNote: Remnants tied to the crime first, then easiest to hardest. They have already rolled, and you are not shown the number - pick what matches what they asked for.
Observe.cardHint: They named what they are looking for and have already rolled; the number is not on this card. Pick a Remnant shows the Remnants where they stand, on your screen alone.
Observe.pickNothing: No Remnant is left that {name} could be shown where they stand. Refuse the Observe from its card.
Observe.pickNotThere: That Remnant is no longer one {name} could be shown where they asked - pick again, or refuse.
Observe.pickGone: Nobody is waiting on this Observe any more: its player stopped waiting, or another GM answered it first.
Observe.describeIntro: {actor} found something in {room}. Name it as they would, and say what they see.
Observe.critPrompt: Critical - the category is identified for them, and they have earned a substantial hint.
Observe.critHintNote: Kept on this student's Truth Bullet only. The trace's description, and everyone else who finds it, never show it.
Observe.resolveLost: {name} rolled {total} on an Observe and this browser has no record of what they were looking at. Nothing was found and nothing was charged - the action is gone. Ask them what they declared, and hand the find over by hand if there was one.
Observe.resolveLostOwner: Your Observe could not be scored: the GM's browser has no record of what you were looking at. Nothing was found and nothing was marked. Tell them what you declared.
