Move.freeAvailable: Your Free Move for this time of day is still there.
Move.freeSpent: Free Move used - the next room costs an action. You have {left}.
Move.nextSprint: Free Move used. The next room takes a free crossing, and your actions stay.
Move.nextBurst: Free Move used. The next room takes your Burst, and your actions stay.

wasSprint.one: Paid by a free crossing. {n} left.
wasSprint.other: Paid by a free crossing. {n} left.

Move.wasFree: That was your Free Move for this time of day.

costAction.one: That cost an action - {left} action left.
costAction.other: That cost an action - {left} actions left.

Move.noBudget: No Free Move and no actions left.
Move.notConnected: {to} is not connected to {from}. From here you can reach: {rooms}
Move.noBudgetLong: No Free Move and no actions left - this crossing was not paid for, so your token was put back.
Move.refundedBack: The GM gave back your last crossing: your token stands where it was before it.
Move.refundedStays: The GM gave back your last crossing, but your token could not be stood where it was before it - ask the GM.
Move.refundedPrice: What the crossing cost is yours again.
Move.refundedNoPrice: The GMs saw nothing it cost, so nothing else came back - ask the GM if it cost you something.
Move.noStairs: No stairs lead from {from} to that floor.
Move.dead: They are dead. The body stays where it fell.

Project.passageRefused: That stretch does not stand between the builder's room and the room beyond: pick it again.
Project.passageNoWall: The builder's room shares no wall with another room on this floor: a secret passage has nowhere to go.
Project.passageNeedsPick: Pick the stretch of wall the secret passage goes through first.
Project.passagePick: Pick the stretch on the wall
Project.passageFrom: From the {room}, where the builder stands.
Project.passageNote: A secret passage through a wall of the room you are in: Hand, Complex (6), always secret. Only you, and whoever the project is shared with before it is finished, will know it.
Project.breachNote: A breach through a wall of the room you are in: Body, Complex (6). Once it is finished the hole is there for everyone to see.
Project.sealNote: Seal the passage: Hand, Complex (6). Once it is finished the passage is closed, for you and for everyone who knows it; a GM can open it again.
Project.unbreachNote: Close the breach: Body, Complex (6). Once it is finished the wall stands whole again.
Project.repairNote: Repair an item: Hand; Trivial (3) for an item of Tier 0 or 1, Complex (6) for Tier 2 or 3. Once it is finished the item is whole again.
Project.repairLockNote: Repair the Lock: Hand, Trivial (3). Once it is finished the lock holds again, for everyone.
Project.notRepaired: {name} is finished, but its item could not be repaired: {why}
Project.needsKiller: An indirect murder needs a killer: pick who it is visible to, or approve it from the proposal card.
Project.needsKillerNamed: “{name}” cannot become an indirect murder from here - open it and name who the trap belongs to.
Project.title: Project
Project.choosePrompt: Start something new, or push a project that already exists?
Project.agreedWarning: Fill this in as your side of the agreement. The GM reads it, may change the scale, the room, or the wording, and only then does the project exist.
Project.startNote: Nothing is created yet. This goes to the GM as a proposal - they approve it, adjust it, or turn it down.
Project.indirectMine: Indirect murder - kept secret, so only you and the GMs see it
Project.traitRequired: A project needs a statistic: pick the one its work demands.
Project.repaired: repaired. {name} can be worked on again.
Project.doneBody: {name} is complete - all {target} progress is in. Ask the GM what it does for you now.
Project.frozenNow: {name} is broken and frozen until {repair} is finished.
Project.alreadyFrozen: {name} is already broken and waiting on a repair.
Project.sabotageNotApplied: The roll succeeded, but no GM confirmed the damage in time. Tell your GM: {name} may not be broken.
Project.none: No projects yet. Start one first.
Project.noneToMove: No project here has progress that can move. Finished ones are done, and a sabotaged one waits for its repair.
Project.aloneBonus: Nobody else is in the room, so the project gains +1 progress.
Project.concealSeen: {actor} is busy with something in {room}, and everyone here can see roughly what.
Project.tracesUncovered: not rolled: the Remnants stay as they were left.
Project.toolRelief: “{item}” is Tier {tier}, so every threshold on this roll comes down by {tier}.
Project.roomOnNoScene: No project was made: {room} is a room on no scene now. Name a room a scene holds, or none.
Project.seenUnknown: Progress unknown: it shows when one of your characters is in this project's room.
Project.seenAsLast: Progress as one of your characters last saw it in this project's room.
Project.cardFrozen: Broken, and frozen until it is repaired
Project.cardSecret: Secret - only the people ticked on it
Project.cardPublic: Public - anyone who has stood in its room
Project.cardShared: Every project token is a copy of this actor. Open a project from its token on the map.
Project.cardUnknown: You do not know what this is.
Project.createNote: Only Work on Project adds progress.
Project.name: Name
Project.visibleToNote: Whoever builds it always sees it.
Project.manageIntro: A project can belong to a room. Only characters standing there can work on it or sabotage it.
Project.secretNote: Indirect murder projects are secret by default: only the killer and the GMs see them. Share to bring in a co-conspirator.
Project.changeImage: Click to change this project's image
Project.tokenMoved: {project} now belongs to {to} - its token was moved there from {from}.

sweptOld.one: {n} project token was left on the map by a project that no longer exists, and has been removed.
sweptOld.other: {n} project tokens were left on the map by projects that no longer exist, and have been removed.

duplicates.one: A project stands on the map twice: {list}. The token the project points at is kept and the spare one is left where it is - delete it by hand if it is a mistake.
duplicates.other: {n} spare project tokens stand beside the ones their projects point at: {list}. Nothing was removed - delete them by hand if they are mistakes.

Project.glyphNote: Under the Stained Glass theme the Projects tray draws this instead of the image, in the interface's color. The image is used everywhere else.
Project.deleteNote: Delete in a project's row asks first, then removes the project for good. Its progress and metadata do not come back.
Project.shareIntro: Let another player see this project. Players can bring in a co-conspirator; GMs can share with anyone.
Project.noPlayers: There are no players to share with.
Project.alreadyFull: {name} is already at {current}/{target}. No progress left to add.
Project.alreadyEmpty: {name} is already at 0. Nothing left to take away.
Project.noneHere: There is no project started in {room}.
Project.allSabotaged: Everything here is already broken or is itself a repair: {names}.
Project.someSabotaged: Not offered - already broken, or a repair project: {names}.
Project.editProgressNote: Progress is kept: this project is at {current}/{target}. Lowering the scale below what is earned clamps it.
Project.deleteConfirm: Delete “{name}”? Its progress goes with it.
Project.conditionPlaceholder: whoever opens the dumbwaiter after dark
Project.conditionNote: Indirect murder only. Name a condition instead of a victim - whoever meets it is who the trap catches.
Project.trapNoCondition: No condition was written down for this trap. Agree one before firing it.
Project.proposalPrompt: Say what you are actually doing and why here. The GM reads this with your answers and decides - they may change the scale, the room or the wording before it starts.
Project.proposalPlaceholder: What you are building, and what you want out of it…
Project.proposerKnows: Your project “{name}” is under way in {room}. It shows on your Projects tray and on the map.
Project.facilityTold: Your project {name} gives a room action: {action}.
Project.sightTold: You are in on the secret project {name}.
Project.sightGone: You are no longer in on a secret project.
Project.facilityGone: Your project {name} no longer gives a room action.
Project.proposalSent: “{name}” has gone to the GM. Nothing starts until they approve it.
Project.proposalNotSent: Nothing was sent to the GM.
Project.declinedPlayer: {name} turned down that project. Talk to them about what would work instead.

workOnHint.one: Push the {n} project running in this room.
workOnHint.other: Push one of the {n} projects running in this room.

Project.startNewHint: Describe something new. Nothing exists until the GM approves it.

sabotageHint.one: Break this room's one breakable project so it needs a repair; you always leave a Remnant.
sabotageHint.other: Break one of this room's {n} projects so it needs a repair; you always leave a Remnant.

Project.alreadyComplete: {name} is finished. There is no work left in it.
Project.allComplete: Every project in {room} is already finished.
Project.frozenNoProgress: {name} has been sabotaged and cannot move forward until its repair is finished.
Project.effectFailed: {name}: part of what finishing it (or taking it back under its target) does could not be done ({error}). The bar stands as it is; the console has the details.
Project.everyone: Public: everyone can see it. Ticked: who knew before it was revealed - they and whoever builds it are who will know if it is sealed again.
Project.builderStays: {name} is building “{project}”: a builder cannot be taken off their own project.
Project.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. A false back in the bookcase, deep enough to hide a notebook
Project.descriptionNote: Everyone who knows the project sees it. At most {max} characters.
Project.descriptionTooLong: A description holds at most {max} characters, and this one has {n}. Shorten it.
Project.trayLessTooltip: Take one point of progress off this project
Project.trayMoreTooltip: Add one point of progress to this project

TraitRuling.title: Which statistic?
TraitRuling.gmBody: This roll can use several statistics. Pick one from what the player says their student does, or refuse.
TraitRuling.waiting: The GM is choosing the statistic. Tell them in your thread what you do.
TraitRuling.refused: The GM turned the action down, so you keep it.
TraitRuling.openingKiller: The GM is choosing the statistic for your opening. Tell them in your thread how you go about it.
TraitRuling.openingKillerProposed: The GM is ruling on the statistic you proposed for your opening.
TraitRuling.openingVictim: The GM is setting up a roll for you.
TraitRuling.gmBodyProposed: The player proposes a statistic. Approve it, change it to another on the list, or refuse.
TraitRuling.changedBody: You proposed {proposed}. The GM changed it to {stat}. You pay nothing unless you roll.
TraitRuling.projectBody: This project was stored without a statistic. Propose one: the GM approves or changes it, and it stays the project's.

DiceLook.setByGm: Your dice look is set by the GM.
DiceLook.settingBack: {name} changed the table's dice look settings, which only a full Gamemaster may change, so they were put back.
DiceLook.settingBackUnheard: The table's dice look settings were changed with no trace of who changed them, and only a full Gamemaster may change them, so they were put back.
DiceLook.stopped: {name}'s dice look keeps changing straight back, so it is left as it is for a minute, then put back at its next change or throw.

diag.title: Dice look
diag.introGm: The dice look as seen here. A player's own look only they can check.
diag.introPlayer: What this browser reads of your dice look. Copy the text at the foot of the window and send it to your GM.
diag.findings: Why the dice may look different

forced.off: not forced: the setting is off

diag.preset: Daggerheart's Hope and Despair dice on this browser
diag.presetNone: none (Daggerheart 2.10 and later color them by Dice So Nice roles)
diag.tableLook: The table's Hope and Despair look, laid on each throw here
diag.lastWindow: Last roll window on this browser
diag.nothingFound: Nothing found that makes this browser draw the dice differently.

finding.notForced: {name} does not hold the table's dice look yet. The primary GM puts it back at their next change or throw.
finding.fuseStopped: {name}'s dice look kept changing back, so it is left as it is for a minute.
finding.overlay: A character of {name}'s carries a dice look of its own: {actors}.
finding.onlyMine: {name} has Dice So Nice's "only my dice" on, so nobody else's dice are drawn on their screen.
finding.othersSfxOff: {name} has other players' special effects switched off.
finding.lowQuality: {name} draws dice at low image quality.
finding.presetDiffers: {duality} of the roll read carries another preset than this browser's Daggerheart setting: it was thrown on another browser.
finding.presetMissing: {duality} of the roll read carries no Daggerheart preset, so it is drawn in its thrower's Dice So Nice look.
finding.presetMissingLaid: {duality} of the roll read carries no Daggerheart preset of its own; with one look for the table, this browser draws it in the table's Hope and Despair look.
finding.presetDiffersLaid: {duality} of the roll read carries another preset than the table's Hope and Despair look; with one look for the table, this browser draws it in the table's look over its own.
finding.missingSystem: Dice So Nice on this browser has no dice system "{name}", so dice that use it are drawn as standard dice here.
finding.missingColorset: Dice So Nice on this browser has no colorset "{name}", so dice that use it are drawn in a custom color here.
finding.missingTexture: Dice So Nice on this browser has no texture "{name}", so dice that use it are drawn with no texture here.
finding.missingMaterial: Dice So Nice on this browser has no material "{name}", so dice that use it are drawn in the automatic material here.
finding.dsnApiMoved: Dice So Nice {version} copies only part of the GM's look; players fill in the rest their own way.
finding.rolesUnforced: Daggerheart {version} colors its Hope and Despair dice by Dice So Nice roles, which the table's forced look does not set.
finding.otherBrowser: {name}'s browser is not read here. Ask them to run game.drpg.diagnoseDiceLook() and send you its text.

RollDialog.locked: Not yours to choose. Advantage and experiences are Hope Calls - ask the GM.
RollDialog.diceFixed: Fixed at d12 by the rules.
RollDialog.advantageLocked: Advantage and disadvantage come from Calls, not from here.
RollDialog.pickOneExperience: Pick the one experience this roll relates to. Clicking another moves the choice.
RollDialog.experienceLocked: Using an experience is the Experience Hope Call - ask the GM to spend it.
RollDialog.bonusLocked: Situational bonuses are the GM's call.
RollDialog.modeLocked: Who sees this roll is set by the game, not here.
RollDialog.modeRoom: The GMs, you and the room
RollDialog.actionLocked: This roll's Hope or Despair decides what happens next, so it is an action, never a reaction.
RollDialog.reactionLocked: A statistic rolled on its own is a reaction: it costs nothing and earns nothing. Hope and Despair come from actions.
RollDialog.unlockedByCall: Unlocked by a Call you paid for.
RollDialog.freeCritArmed: Loaded Die is armed. One of the two dice, at random, is set to 12 and the other is thrown - a very high total, and a critical only if that one comes up 12 as well.
RollDialog.forcedByCall: Set by a Call you paid for. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.forcedByHindrance: A hindrance die is on this roll. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.forcedBySituation: Set by where you are and what you are looking for. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.forcedByState: You are in Breakdown - every roll is at disadvantage until some Sanity comes back. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.lockedByCall: A Call has already decided this roll's modifier.
RollDialog.stackedAdvantage: Advantage ×{n} - {sources}. You roll {n} bonus dice and the best one counts. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.stackedDisadvantage: Disadvantage ×{n} - {sources}. You roll {n} penalty dice and the worst one counts. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.mixedAdvantage: Advantage - {sources}. Together that is one bonus die. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.mixedDisadvantage: Disadvantage - {sources}. Together that is one penalty die. It cannot be turned off.

advantageCapped.one: More than {cap} die stops being a roll, so it stops at {cap}.
advantageCapped.other: More than {cap} dice stops being a roll, so it stops at {cap}.

what.despair.all: Filling or emptying every Despair pool
what.despair.roster: Granting, revoking, or naming a Despair pool
what.passage.lairSeal: Seal a passage at your door
what.token.refundCrossing: Give back a character's last crossing
what.monocub.answer: The answer to the Monocub invitation
what.call.arm: A Call bought for a roll
what.remnant.tieForItem: Tie a Remnant to the crime
what.observe.pick: A GM's pick for a focused Observe
what.cleanup.ruling: A GM's ruling on a reshaped Remnant
what.call.yes: A GM's yes to a Hope Call
what.dynamic.answer: A GM's ruling on a Dynamic Action
what.ruling.expired: A ruling you stopped waiting for
what.trait.ruling: The GM's pick of a statistic
what.roll.subject: A report of whose roll it was
what.roll.bookmark: What a roll did, kept for a Reroll
what.roll.draw: A roll for the GM to throw
what.roll.grant: A grant of rolls thrown with no GM connected
what.audit.decide: A GM's decision on a sheet change flagged to the GMs
what.keys.charge: The Key fee charged as a Class Trial opens
what.trial.enter: The Class Trial's voices settled as it opens or ends
what.trial.record: A GM's write of the Class Trial's record, made by the primary GM
what.card.post: A card for the GM to post
what.card.claim: A GM's ruling on a card sent to the GMs
what.bullet.give: A Truth Bullet a GM gives
what.searchTokens.returnToken: Give back a Search Token spent too late
what.floor.now: The floor's next step now, run on the primary GM
what.vote.run: A step of the vote, run on the primary GM
what.trial.evidence: Put your Truth Bullet on the Objection
what.trial.gm: A GM's change to the trial's floor, run on the primary GM
what.advancement.offers: Level Up offers to choose from
what.bridge.done: A GM's answer to your request
what.bridge.gmReady: A GM back at the table
what.bridge.refused: A GM's refusal of your request
what.bridge.ack: A GM's word that your request arrived
what.trial.side: Picking a side in the trial hall
what.ready.open: Asking the players whether they are done
what.ready.end: Ending the question to the players

Bridge.nothingSpent: You keep your action and your Hope.
Bridge.emptyRequest: Nothing was sent - write your request first.

why.unknownSender: The GM does not see you as connected. Reload and try again.
why.notYours: It names a character you do not play.
why.gmOnly: Only a GM can ask for that.
why.missing: What it names is not there any more.
why.badRequest: The GM's side could not read that request.
why.outOfRange: A number in it is out of range.
why.busy: It is already being written. Wait a moment and look again.
why.notOffered: No Level Up is on offer for that character.
why.notSecret: Only a secret project can be shared.
why.notAPlayer: A project can only be shared with a player.
why.notHolding: None of your characters in the fight holds that object.
why.alreadyHeld: That character already holds that Call.
why.notASupport: That Call cannot be bought for that character.
why.hopeBarred: You cannot spend a Hope Call right now.
why.notEnoughHope: The character paying does not hold enough Hope.
why.noReroll: Only a Reroll of that character's roll from the last few minutes can take it back.
why.undoIsTheGms: Taking a result back is the GM's: a Reroll is asked of the GM, who takes the first result back.
why.traceOutOfReach: A Reroll can no longer reach that Remnant.
why.notInIncident: Your character is not in a running incident.
why.actionLocked: That action is locked for now.
why.actionSpent: You have already taken that one this incident.
why.actionBlocked: They have shut this one down for now.
why.actionDenied: That action is not open to that character now.
why.nothingLeft: There is nothing left to spend.
why.movedOn: The incident has moved on since that action.
why.notThatRepair: That is not the repair your sabotage made.
why.notWhereItStood: The token did not stand there a moment ago.
why.nothingToUndo: There is nothing of that to take back.
why.deathStands: That crisis action killed somebody: the death stands, and it cannot be taken back.
why.notThere: The character is not where it needs to be.
why.relay: This game leaves that change to the GM.
why.failed: It failed on the GM's side; the GM can see the details.
why.noAnswer: The GM's client did not answer in time.
why.capReached: That student has had a Monocub's move this time of day. You keep your action and Hope.
why.capDay: That student has had two Monocub moves today. You keep your action and Hope.
why.answerKeyMissing: The GM's browser does not hold this bullet's answer key. The GM has been told.
why.keysNotOpen: The GM's browser has not opened the answer keys yet. The GM has been told.
why.rollUnknown: The GM's client holds no roll of yours that it could be scored on.
why.rollNotYours: The roll it names is not your character's.
why.rollOtherAction: The roll it names was thrown for another action.
why.rollUsed: That roll has already been scored.
why.rollStale: The roll it names is too old to be scored.
why.rollMissed: The roll it names did not earn that.
why.projectFrozen: That project is frozen by a sabotage until its repair is finished.
why.rollReplaced: A later roll of the same action replaced the roll it names.
why.notPaid: No action was paid for that roll. Take the action again.
why.rollThrown: That action's roll has been thrown already.
why.callNotPaid: No Hope was paid for that Call.
why.callNotApproved: That Call has no yes from a GM. Ask for it again.
why.itemNotDecided: No GM has decided yet on that item, which a player made on a sheet: it changes no hands until one does.
why.notEligible: You hold no ballot in this vote.
why.wrongCount: Your ballot does not name as many people as the vote asks for.
why.sheetPutBack: That change to your sheet was undone: no action in the game accounts for it.
why.notKnown: You do not know that secret passage.
why.recipientDead: The one you chose is dead. Nothing was shown.
why.floorClosed: The debate is not open to an Objection now.
why.noSpeaker: Nobody has spoken in this trial yet, so there is nobody to object to.
why.noBullet: You hold no Truth Bullet to prove an Objection with.
why.objectionOver: That Objection is no longer waiting for a Truth Bullet.
why.notAtPassage: Stand on the passage's mark, or a square next to it, first.
why.oneWay: This passage cannot be taken from this side.
why.roomSealed: That room is sealed for this time of day. Nobody gets in.
why.onWatch: You keep watch: you stay at your post until the Eclipse ends.
why.chained: You are chained here until this time of day ends.
why.cannotLeave: You are in an incident. The only way out is a crisis action - Survive, Escape Together, a Finishing Blow, or, if you only walked in on it, Averted Eyes.
why.trialLocked: The Class Trial is in session. Nobody leaves the courtroom until it ends.
why.noBudget: No Free Move and no actions left.
why.eclipseSpent: Your Eclipse crossings are used up.
why.roundMovedOn: The GM is asking again: answer the new question.
why.notInRound: This question is for the players whose students are in play, and yours is not.

Bridge.criticalHint: Critical - this player is owed a substantial hint.
Bridge.declined: {name} turned the attempt down. Your action is back.
Bridge.declinedGm: Turned down. {name} has the action back.
Bridge.settledExpired: Nobody answered in time - ask again.
Bridge.settledGone: The player was no longer waiting.
Bridge.settledUnconfirmed: Answered by {name} - not confirmed as received.
Bridge.claimBusy: {gm} is ruling on this card right now.
Bridge.alreadySettled: This card has already been answered.
Bridge.replyPrompt: Your ruling, in your own words. It goes into their thread.
Bridge.createItemStays: Create an item leaves this card open, so the other answers stay available.

Tables.installed: Item tables ready: {created} created, {skipped} already existed.

allPresent.one: {n} item table already exists in this world.
allPresent.other: All {n} item tables already exist in this world.

Tables.rebuildNote: Rebuilding deletes them and builds them again from the module's own lists. Anything you edited by hand is lost.

someFailed.one: {n} item table could not be created. See the console.
someFailed.other: {n} item tables could not be created. See the console.

Tables.whereNote: A Search draws from the room's tables first, then from the tier pools.
Tables.noRoomPools: No room pools yet. Name one below.
Tables.newTierPoolNote: A tier pool is named for its category and its tier, as “DRPG Tools - Tier 2” is. Usually you do not make one by hand: “Install / reinstall” below builds them all.
Tables.newTierPoolForms: “{name}” is not a tier pool. Name it for a category and a tier, one of: {forms} - where N is a tier from {low} to {high}.
Tables.renameOtherPool: “{name}” would name another pool. This one holds the items of “{pool}”: keep its category and tier in the name.
Tables.installTabNote: “Install / reinstall” below builds the default set - one table per category and tier. If they already exist, you choose between keeping yours and rebuilding.
Tables.editorIntro: Everything a Search can turn up. Pick a table on the left.
Tables.roomBreakdown: Sorted by what the tier pools say each name is. A flat room table still answers whatever category a Search asks for - name a table "Room - Murder Weapons" to have that decided here instead.
Tables.unfiledNote: No tier pool holds these names, so the module cannot say what they are or how good they are. In a flat room table they can come up for any category. Use the arrows on a row to put one in a tier pool.
Tables.placeIntro: Tick every pool this item should be in. Ticking a new one copies it there, unticking one takes it out, and unticking the pool you are looking at moves it.
Tables.placeRolesNote: The description, the picture, and the roles travel with it. A tier pool below Tier 2 takes no roles, and no pool takes a role that is its own category.
Tables.placeNone: An item has to live in at least one pool. Use the row's ✕ to delete it outright.
Tables.placeUnchanged: {name} is already in exactly those pools.
Tables.noneYet: No item tables yet - create the default set below.
Tables.tierTargetIs: Goes into {table}. Worked out from the category and tier above.
Tables.tierTargetNone: No such tier pool - the item turns up only in the rooms ticked. Install the pools on the Tier pools tab.
Tables.roomTargets: Room tables it also appears in:
Tables.noRoomTables: No room tables yet - create one on the Room pools tab.
Tables.rolesTierOnly: Two jobs start at tier {tier} - an item this cheap does one.
Tables.rolesNote: What else it can be. It still takes one slot.
Tables.addNote: The finder gets the icon and the description.
Tables.needsTable: Pick a tier table or tick at least one room table.
Tables.newPoolNote: What a room stocks. Assign it in Room setup, the “Draws from” column.
Tables.newPoolTierName: That name matches the tier-table pattern (“DRPG … - Tier N”) - a room table needs its own name.
Tables.presetRoomNoTable: {room} draws from no table of its own. Point it at one in Room setup to keep finds like this there.
Tables.presetRoomTier: {room} has no table for this tier yet: make “{name}” on the Room pools tab to keep finds of this tier there.
Tables.tierPoolCreated: "{name}" is ready, and the module recognized it: items in it are filed by its category and tier, so a usable drawn from it knows what it does.
Tables.poolCreated: Room table “{name}” created. Point a room at it in Room setup.
Tables.renameNote: A tier pool keeps a name of its category and tier. A room table can take any other name.

deleteConfirm.one: Delete “{name}” and the {n} entry in it? This cannot be undone.
deleteConfirm.other: Delete “{name}” and the {n} entries in it? This cannot be undone.

Clock.rewindDuringEclipse: An Eclipse is running. End it first.
Clock.takenBack: Taken back: the actions, the Free Moves, the Search Tokens, and the seals are as they were before this time of day began.
Clock.eclipseStillOn: The clock moved, but the Eclipse is still running. End it from the clock's chevron when you are ready - until then tokens place freely and murders are refused.

GiveBack.title: Give back Foundry's settings
GiveBack.intro: While it runs, this module changes these settings of Foundry, Daggerheart, and the modules it needs:

what.automation: Daggerheart's Vulnerable and Defeated automations are off: Breakdown and Wounded take their place.
what.playerFiles: Players and Trusted Players cannot browse or upload files ('Keep players out of the file browser').
what.isoWelcome: Isometric Perspective's welcome window stays closed for everyone.
what.dhWelcome: Daggerheart's welcome journal does not open for anyone.
what.liveKitInFoundry: LiveKit's voice stays inside the Foundry window for everyone.
what.rtcDock: Foundry's camera dock is folded while the voice tile is on, and no camera pops out.
what.sceneVision: On scenes with rooms, the rooms take over Foundry's own vision, fog, and global light: turning 'Rooms decide what players can see' off gives them back.
what.diceLook: With one look for the table in 'Dice look for the table', every player and Assistant GM throws Dice So Nice dice in one full Gamemaster's look. Give back does not change this, and nobody's own earlier look comes back: the module never kept it.

GiveBack.filesStay: Give back leaves the file permissions as they are now: if players should browse or upload files, grant it in Foundry's permissions.

Give them back sets Daggerheart's defaults - both on. If this world had them off, switch them off again in Daggerheart's settings.

Reroll.passageStands: The passage find stands: new dice do not open it twice.

Reroll.nothingToReroll: You have not rolled anything, so there is nothing to take back.
Reroll.notARoll: Your last message carries no dice.
Reroll.failed: The reroll could not be applied. Tell the GM.
Reroll.despairGained: The new result is a Despair result: {name} gains 1 Despair.
Reroll.despairReturned: The old result was a Despair result: 1 Despair is returned to {name}.
Reroll.critHopeGained: The new result is a critical: you gain the second point of Hope a crit is worth.
Reroll.critHopeReturned: The old result was a critical: the second point of Hope it paid is taken back.

infiltrate.tail: Rerolled: the tail's strength is now {n}.

infiltrate.shutGone: Rerolled: the barricade is down already, so nothing changes.
infiltrate.forceStands: Rerolled: the door was forced by the first roll and stays forced.
infiltrate.forceRefused: Rerolled: the door cannot be tried again from here.
infiltrate.forced: Rerolled: the door gives way now.
infiltrate.pickStands: Rerolled: the lock was picked by the first roll and the picker has gone through, so it stands.
infiltrate.pickTaken: Rerolled: the lock holds after all, and the way in the first roll opened is gone.
infiltrate.pickRefused: Rerolled: the lock cannot be tried again from here.
infiltrate.picked: Rerolled: the lock gives now, and the picker may walk in.
infiltrate.watchStands: Rerolled: a watch can no longer be set, so the first roll's stands.
infiltrate.facilityStands: Rerolled: the room action succeeded the first time and its effects stand.
infiltrate.facilityGone: Rerolled: the room action is no longer here, so nothing changes.
infiltrate.facilityMissed: Rerolled: the room action still fails.
infiltrate.facility: Rerolled: the room action succeeds now.

Reroll.noReplay: Nothing but the dice to take back: this roll left no lasting effect.
Reroll.replayFailed: The dice were rerolled, but the action could not be replayed. Tell the GM what the first roll had already done.
Reroll.observeReplayed: The same trace goes back to the GM with the new roll. They will say what you find this time.
Reroll.analyzeReplayed: The same Truth Bullet is analyzed again with the new roll. Any lock the first attempt left is lifted first.
Reroll.crisisReplayed: The crisis action is taken back and made again with the new roll - the damage, the Remnant, and any hindrance go with it. The turn is not spent twice.
Reroll.deathStands: A crisis action that killed cannot be taken back: the death stands.
Reroll.busy: A Reroll of this character is already being made. Wait for it to finish.
Reroll.messageGone: The roll is no longer in the chat, so there is nothing to throw again. You keep your Hope.
Reroll.interrupted: {name}'s Reroll was cut short by a reload before its new dice counted. The first roll stands, and the Hope paid for it is given back.
Reroll.interruptedGm: {name}'s Reroll ({action}) was cut short by a reload while its action was being taken back and made again. The first roll was {first}, the new one {total}; the card shows the new one. What the first roll did may be undone only in part: check by hand what this action leaves - progress, items, Remnants, damage, a turn - and settle it. The Hope stays paid, and this roll cannot be rerolled again.
Reroll.interruptedPending: {name}'s Reroll was cut short by a reload while it was being made. The GM will settle it; the Hope stays paid.
Reroll.interruptedPaying: {name}'s Reroll was cut short by a reload while its {cost} Hope was being paid, before the dice were thrown again. The first roll stands and can still be rerolled. Check {name}'s Hope by hand: the payment may or may not have been written.
Reroll.interruptedGivingBack: {name}'s Reroll did not stand, and a reload cut short the giving back of its {cost} Hope. The first roll is back on the card and can still be rerolled. Check {name}'s Hope by hand: it may or may not have come back.
Reroll.interruptedHope: {name}'s Reroll was cut short by a reload. The first roll stands; the GM will check the Hope.
Reroll.stillMaking: The GM did not answer the Reroll in time, but it may still be made: if it is, its card follows; if it is not, its Hope is not taken.
Reroll.observeBusy: The GM is still describing what this Observe found. Reroll it once the result is in. You keep your Hope.
Reroll.diceChanged: This roll's dice are not the ones the GMs kept: a change to them is being put back. Reroll it in a moment. You keep your Hope.
Reroll.trailStands: The dice are rewritten, but what you planted is already lying in the room - a reroll cannot pick it back up. Ask the GM if it should come out.
Reroll.authorsCopyBack: The new dice take back the Truth Bullet of the Remnant you left.
Reroll.stealStands: The dice are rewritten, but the moment is not. Your hand has already been in their pocket, and putting something back is something they would watch you do.
Reroll.friskStands: The dice are rewritten, but the moment is not. The whole room saw how it went.
Reroll.rummageStands: The dice are rewritten, but the moment is not. They already know whether you got a proper look.
Reroll.rummageSeen: The dice are rewritten, but what you saw stays seen.
Reroll.rummageLate: The moment has passed: {who} is no longer within reach.
Reroll.cleanupReplayed: The clean-up is taken back and attempted again. The Remnant comes back, anything the botched wipe left is removed, and the Sanity is refunded first.
Reroll.itemTakenBack: “{item}” is taken back out of your inventory.
Reroll.itemStuck: “{item}” could not be removed automatically - ask the GM to take it.
Reroll.stashFound: The new result opens a hidden stash: its card says whose.
Reroll.tokenKept: The room's Search Token stays spent - the room was searched either way.
Reroll.remnantRetuned: The Remnant you left has been adjusted to match.
Reroll.remnantLeft: The new result leaves a Remnant behind.
Reroll.remnantRemoved: The Remnant the first roll left is removed.
Reroll.remnantManual: The Remnant the first roll left cannot be adjusted from here - ask the GM to re-rate it.
Reroll.traceKept: {name}'s Reroll left the Remnant of the first roll as it was ({trace}): a GM has written on it or set its band, a Reroll put it back, it is too old for a Reroll to reach, or - where the new result would have removed it - somebody has already found it. The console says which. If the new result ({total}) should change it, re-rate or remove it by hand.
Reroll.sabotageUndone: The first attempt is undone: the target is unfrozen and its repair project removed.
Reroll.sabotageRedone: {name} breaks again - the repair now needs {n} progress.
Reroll.sabotageNowFails: The new result fails: the target is left working.
Reroll.actionTakenBack: The critical is gone, so the action it returned is spent again.
Reroll.actionOwed: The critical is gone, but the action it returned is already used. You owe one.
Reroll.gmReasked: The GM has been asked to rule again on the new result.
Reroll.rulingVoid: Rerolled: {old} no longer stands, the result is now {new}. Rule again.
Reroll.lootStands: The dice are rewritten, but the moment is not. What you took is in your hands, and the body looks as it did.

phase.eclipse: The lights are out. Everyone places their token - {reach}, or anywhere at night - and nobody can see who went where. Your actions are already refilled, but nothing spends them except a Direct Murder, and nobody makes a Call until the lights come up. It is the game's one moment of total cover, and it is where a murder usually starts.
phase.dailyLife: Ordinary days inside the school. You have {actions} each time of day, unless your sheet says otherwise, to search rooms, work on projects, rest, talk, and prepare. Nobody has died yet this chapter - this is the part where you decide who you trust.
phase.investigation: A body has been found. Observe Remnants on the map, Analyze what you collect, and every Truth Bullet you build is one you can present at the trial. What you fail to find, you will not have.
phase.classTrial: Everyone is in the room and one of you did it. Testimony, Objections, and finally the vote. Get it right and the killer is punished; get it wrong and everybody else is.

time.what: Actions refill at the start of each one, and each room's Search Tokens come back with them. When the last one ends, the day turns over.

despair.title: What Despair is
despair.what: Despair is the GM side's currency. It fills when rolls at the table come up with Despair rather than Hope - which is to say, it is fed by your bad luck and your risks.
despair.spent: It is spent on Despair Calls: the moves that make life harder - pushing a scene, hardening a room, turning a screw. The more of it there is, the more the school can do to you.
despair.masked: Every pool's count is public - the rows show how full each one is. Only the overflow's count is hidden from you.
despair.noPools: No Monokuma has a pool yet.

status.actionsWhat: {actions} each time of day. Searching a room, working on a project, observing a trace, analyzing a Truth Bullet - each of those is one. A Short Rest costs {short}, a Long Rest {long}.
status.actionsWounded: With no Health left you get {wounded} instead of {actions} in Daily Life and the Investigation, until somebody patches you up. In the Class Trial, Wounded takes no action.
status.actionsNow: You have {left} of {max} left this time of day.
status.moveWhat: One move between rooms each time of day that costs you nothing. After that, changing rooms costs an action like anything else.
status.moveSpent: Your Free Move is gone this time of day - moving now costs an action.
status.hopeWhat: Hope is yours, and it is spent on Hope Calls: helping somebody else's roll, leaning on an Experience, invoking your Ultimate, rerolling. It comes back when rolls go your way.
status.monokumaActions: You have no action economy. A Monokuma is skipped when actions are refilled, and spends none.
status.monokumaMove: Movement costs you nothing and grants you nothing - there is no Free Move to keep track of.
status.monokumaDespair: You spend Despair where a student spends Hope. The pools are at the top of the screen.
status.monokumaWalls: Walls and locked doors do not apply to you.

projects.title: What a project is
projects.what: A project is something that takes longer than one action: building it, fixing it, poisoning it, digging through it. Each one lives in a room and only moves when somebody works on it there.
projects.progress: Working on a project is an action, and a roll - how well it goes decides how much progress it takes. When the bar fills, the thing is done.
projects.secret: Some projects are private to the people working on them. If you cannot see one, it is not on your list.
projects.none: Nothing yet - no project is visible to you.

unnamed.why: Rooms are matched by name, so a region with none is not a room: it never counts as a neighbor, which is one quiet way to get a doorway that leads nowhere.

defaultName.problem: Room still has the name Foundry gave it
defaultName.why: A room is its name: players read it on the map, and keys, stashes, and Room setup all name it. Give it the room's own name before play.

piecesDiffer.problem: Pieces of this room are set up differently
piecesDiffer.why: A room drawn in several pieces reads each setting from the first piece that has it, so another piece's setting is not the room's. In Room setup change the room's setting, Apply, then set it back and Apply: that gives every piece the same. Set the height in each piece's region settings.

noShape.problem: No geometry the fog can read
noShape.why: The region exists but its shape came back empty: nothing about this room will be drawn.

overlap.title: Rooms overlap
overlap.fact: About {squares} squares of floor belong to both rooms.
overlap.deep: About {squares} squares of floor belong to both rooms, reaching {depth} squares in.
overlap.why: Where two rooms overlap, one room's border runs across the other's floor with no wall near it, and the whole shared border reads as one doorway. Rooms should touch; a sliver thinner than a quarter square is ignored.

adrift.problem: Border runs away from the walls
adrift.fact: {squares} squares of border with no wall.
adrift.why: A border drawn away from the wall it stands for turns that whole side of the room into a doorway: the wall is never found, so nothing closes it.

sealed.title: No way out: walled all round
sealed.fact: Every stretch of the border is walled.
sealed.why: Nothing glows as a doorway. If the room is sealed on purpose, leave it; if not, the door is missing.

isolated.title: No way out: no room beside it
isolated.fact: No room within a square of the border.
isolated.why: The next room is more than a square away, so the two never meet at a doorway. Rooms should touch along the edge they share.

lattice.problem: Corners off the map's own lattice
lattice.why: The rest of the map is drawn to a half-square lattice. Draw with snapping on: a corner a fraction of a square out cannot be seen by eye and is enough to make two rooms overlap or miss.

Case.backupWhat: The file holds every GM-only secret of this world: who the Mastermind is, every Truth Bullet's answer, every Remnant's real type, the cast of an open incident and the Blackened of each chapter, the traps' planted objects, the Level Ups on offer and the rooms each character has found. Keep it where no player can open it.
Case.backupEarly: The copy from {names} has not arrived yet: this backup holds only what this browser has. Back up anyway?

backedUp.one: The case was saved to a file: {n} row.
backedUp.other: The case was saved to a file: {n} rows.

Case.chapterReminder: The answer keys this chapter's close reveals live in GM browsers, not in the world file. Back up the case: {when}.

refused.unreadable: That file is not a case backup.
refused.newer: That file was written by a newer version of the module (format {version}); this one cannot read it.
refused.otherWorld: That file is the case of another world ({title}). Tick the box to restore it here anyway.
refused.malformed: That file cannot be restored: its section for {store} is damaged (the console names the row). Nothing was changed.

Case.restoredStore: {store}: {n} changed, {cut} under the reset's cut left out

store.passageMap: The secret passages: where each one is and whether it is open
store.passageAccess: Who knows each secret passage, and how they learnt it
store.passageLog: What was done with the secret passages
store.passageSeason: The secret passages a project made this season
store.observe: The Observe declarations waiting for their roll
store.discovery: The rooms each character has found
store.projectSecrets: Who builds each trap, and what sets it off
store.foundDone: The finished secret projects waiting for their finders to come back
store.pendingMurders: The Direct Murders declared in the dark
store.eclipseMoves: Who has crossed how often in the Eclipse
store.keyPlan: The Key Remnant plan, chapter by chapter
store.trialCast: Which of the trial hall's tokens the trial shows
store.caseSchema: The case map: each chapter's deductions, counters, and solution
store.deaths: The deaths nobody has found yet
store.deferredOffers: The Reinforced Level Ups waiting for the class
store.despairOwed: The Despair each pool owes for its conversions to Hope
store.lootTraces: What has been taken off each body, and its trace
store.lootRolls: The first Hand and Shadow roll each taker made for their next Take from each body
store.rifles: Which stash each character has gone through, and in which time of day
store.facilityUses: Which room actions each character used, and in which time of day
store.tails: Who is tailing whom today, and how well
store.barricades: Which rooms are barricaded, by whom and how strongly
store.bedroomNotes: What happened to each bedroom while its owner was away, told when they walk back in
store.watches: Who keeps watch through the Eclipse, from which room, and what they saw
store.pendingBodies: The bodies found that wait for the GMs' word to be announced
store.bodiesHeard: Which bodies each character has heard the discovery sound for
store.lockpicks: Who may walk through a lock they picked, into which room
store.eavesdrops: Who listens at which door, from which room, and which room they may listen at again for free
store.masks: Which killer hides behind a "?" after a murder's opening, and what their token looked like
store.timedEffects: What room actions gave each character for a while, and when it ends
store.clockBeat: When the primary GM was last at the table, so the gap between two sessions is no time of day
store.takeBack: What the last start of a time of day gave, for five minutes, so a misclick can be taken back
store.crossings: Each character's last crossing between rooms, what it cost, and whether a GM gave it back
store.traceDigest: The traces placed since the last digest to the GMs, said at the next time of day
store.confusions: The Confusions armed on a character and not rolled yet
store.cubs: The Monocubs' record: which Monocub witnessed the crime
store.cubTargets: How many Monocub moves each student has had this day
store.projectWork: Who worked on each project this time of day
store.bounties: The open Bounties on students, for the Monocubs
store.rerollBookmarks: Each character's last roll a Reroll would take back, and what the GMs did for it
store.cleanupAttempts: Each character's last clean-up, kept so a Reroll can take it back
store.rerollJournal: A Reroll the GM is making, step by step, so a reload in the middle can be put right
store.rolls: The players' rolls the GM threw, with their dice and totals, for the resolutions and Rerolls that read them
store.usedTools: The Cleaning Tools each clean-up used, broken when the body is found
store.sheetMarks: What each character's sheet held when the GMs last judged a write on it
store.sheetWrites: The writes on a student's sheet the GMs put back, flagged, or listed, kept a day
store.diceLooks: Each character's dice look as the GMs set it, which a player's change of it goes back to
store.ballots: The ballots of the Class Trial's vote, kept by the GMs
store.verdict: The Blackened the last verdict was given with, kept by the GMs for its Finish
store.trialMute: The microphones the Class Trial turned off, and what each player had before, kept by the GMs until it ends
store.closingClaim: Who volunteered for the Closing Argument, and who was drawn, kept by the GMs
store.ruledCards: Who ruled each card sent to the GMs, so a card is ruled once
store.caseTicks: The trial's ticks: each chapter's deductions, counters and solution a GM ticked
store.diveSets: Logic Dive sets: each set's questions, their answers and which answer is right

traces.one: {n} Remnant on the map (of {of}) has no answer key on this browser.
traces.other: {n} Remnants on the map (of {of}) have no answer key on this browser.

bullets.one: {n} Truth Bullet (of {of}) has no answer key on this browser: an Analyze of it is refused.
bullets.other: {n} Truth Bullets (of {of}) have no answer key on this browser: an Analyze of them is refused.

noAnswer.one: {n} answer key has lost its real type (the damage the old merge did).
noAnswer.other: {n} answer keys have lost their real type (the damage the old merge did).

row.incident: An incident is open, and this browser does not hold its cast.
row.neverHeld: This browser has never held this world's case, which began on {date}.
row.legacyChanged: The old store of {store} changed after the upgrade (a GM went back to an older version): take what changed from the diagnostics.
row.claimFailed: This browser's old {store} could not be taken over: {error}. Nothing was changed; the next load tries again.
row.unseen: This check cannot see who the Mastermind is, the Level Up offers or the Blackened register: a browser that lost them does not know it.

left.one: {n} old row stays in this browser, not taken: another world's, or no longer part of this world's case.
left.other: {n} old rows stay in this browser, not taken: other worlds', or no longer part of this world's case.

clamped.one: {n} old row was stamped after the moment this browser took it over - a clock that ran ahead - and was taken at that moment.
clamped.other: {n} old rows were stamped after the moment this browser took them over - a clock that ran ahead - and were taken at that moment.

row.skew: Stamps from ahead of this browser's clock: {names}.
row.bytes: The GM stores take {stores} KB of this browser's storage; the module {total} KB in all, its notice history aside.
row.notices: The notice history takes {notices} KB of this browser's storage besides: when the storage is full, it gives its room back to the case's stores and the private cards.
row.neverBackedUp: This case has never been backed up.

traceOrphans.one: {n} Remnant's answer key has no token on any scene: kept, and read by nothing.
traceOrphans.other: {n} Remnants' answer keys have no token on any scene: kept, and read by nothing.

row.mastermindCleared: A GM's old store (from before 1.2.63) says the Mastermind was cleared on {cleared}, after {name} was picked on {picked} - possibly in another world. Until a GM decides, that player is not told they hold the part. Keep the pick, or clear it.

traps.one: {n} armed item trap has no planted object on this browser: it cannot fire.
traps.other: {n} armed item traps have no planted object on this browser: they cannot fire.

projectSecrets.one: {n} indirect murder (of {of}) has no killer, condition or trigger on this browser: its trap cannot arm or fire.
projectSecrets.other: {n} indirect murders (of {of}) have no killer, condition or trigger on this browser: their traps cannot arm or fire.

notes.one: {n} pre-session note is marked written, and this browser does not hold it, or holds an older one.
notes.other: {n} pre-session notes are marked written, and this browser does not hold them, or holds older ones.

tracesOnToken.one: {n} Remnant on the map (of {of}) still carries its answer key on its token: it is moved into the ledger, not restored.
tracesOnToken.other: {n} Remnants on the map (of {of}) still carry their answer keys on their tokens: they are moved into the ledger, not restored.

tracesKept.one: {n} Remnant on the map (of {of}) keeps flags of its answer key on its token, which every browser holds - a Faint Prep promotion a later correction stood against, or flags with no ledger row to carry them into: a GM decides it, and game.drpg.migrateRemnants() names it.
tracesKept.other: {n} Remnants on the map (of {of}) keep flags of their answer keys on their tokens, which every browser holds - a Faint Prep promotion a later correction stood against, or flags with no ledger row to carry them into: a GM decides each, and game.drpg.migrateRemnants() names them.

leftNotPrimary.one: {n} of this world's old offers or fog rows stays in this browser: only the primary GM's browser takes them. With this world open here as the primary, game.drpg.gmStoreReclaim takes it (the diagnostics name the store).
leftNotPrimary.other: {n} of this world's old offers or fog rows stay in this browser: only the primary GM's browser takes them. With this world open here as the primary, game.drpg.gmStoreReclaim takes them (the diagnostics name the store).

Case.healthIntro: This browser is missing part of this world's case:
Case.healthNote: Restore brings it back from a backup file; Continue carries on without it, and the GM panel keeps saying so until the case is whole.
Case.continued: The case is incomplete on this browser. Restore it from a backup file (GM panel, Diagnostics, The case: Restore from a file).
Case.panelWarning: The case is incomplete on this browser:
Case.previewStore: {store}: {add} new, {refresh} refreshed, {kept} newer here, {cut} under the reset's cut, {remove} removed here
Case.otherWorld: This file is the case of another world ({title}). Restore it here anyway.
Case.beforeCut: Restore anyway the rows the last reset removed (they come back freshly stamped).
Case.restoreNote: A restore takes only what is newer than what this browser holds - a removal too, counted above. It never takes the file's reset cut, and a file of another world brings no removal.
Case.answerKeyMissing: {actor}'s Truth Bullet "{bullet}" has no answer key on this browser, so its Analyze was refused. Restore it from a backup (GM panel, Diagnostics, The case: Restore from a file).

chargeHeld.one: The charge for unfound Key Remnants is held: {n} Truth Bullet has no answer key on this browser, and the count would come out wrong. Restore it from a backup (GM panel, Diagnostics, The case) and ask again.
chargeHeld.other: The charge for unfound Key Remnants is held: {n} Truth Bullets have no answer key on this browser, and the count would come out wrong. Restore them from a backup (GM panel, Diagnostics, The case) and ask again.

filled.one: {n} Truth Bullet took its answer key from its Remnant.
filled.other: {n} Truth Bullets took their answer keys from their Remnants.

Case.decideIntro: One thing in this world needs a GM to decide it:
Case.castIntro: An incident is running and this browser does not know who is in it. Name them as they are at the table; a GM who held the cast and comes back later brings it with them.
Case.castThird: A third, if there was one
Case.previewRecord: {store}: another world's - taken only if you tick it below.

previewClamped.one: {n} row is stamped later than the clock allows: it would be taken at this moment.
previewClamped.other: {n} rows are stamped later than the clock allows: they would be taken at this moment.

previewNotThisWorld.one: {n} row is another world's and is left out.
previewNotThisWorld.other: {n} rows are another world's and are left out.

Case.otherWorldRecord: Take {store} from this file as well: another world's, it replaces this world's where the file's is newer.

restoredClamped.one: {n} row was stamped later than the clock allows and was taken at this moment.
restoredClamped.other: {n} rows were stamped later than the clock allows and were taken at this moment.

Case.moveNote: Move them into the ledger takes each Remnant's answer key off its token (game.drpg.migrateRemnants); Continue carries on without it, and the GM panel keeps saying so until the case is whole.

CaseMap.autopsyWhen: Goes to every living student when body {n} is found.

autopsyWentOut.one: The planned Autopsy Truth Bullet went out to {n} student.
autopsyWentOut.other: The planned Autopsy Truth Bullet went out to {n} students.

CaseMap.removeAsk: Remove {name} from the case? A node that rests on it keeps naming it, and the check says so.
CaseMap.notSaved: Not saved. Your text is still in the fields.
CaseMap.culpritOnly: Only the culprit holds it, so it does not count.

problem.cycle: {node} is on a circle of inputs, so the map leaves it out.
problem.noSolution: The case has deductions and no solution.
problem.solutionUnreached: Nothing on the map leads to {node}.
problem.badMode: {node} asks for a trial mode the trial does not have, “{ref}”.
problem.culpritOnly: Only the culprit holds {ref}, an input of {node}, so it does not count.
problem.tooManyKeys: Key Remnants in the case: {ref}, more than a chapter prepares.

CaseMap.finalAskRoomTitle: Where does the Final Truth Remnant go?

CaseRealize.title: Realization of the case, chapter {chapter}
CaseRealize.intro: Nothing changes until you press Run realization. Each Key Remnant slot not on the map yet is placed in the room you pick; a slot with no room stays as it is.
CaseRealize.undoNote: Undo realization removes only what nobody has found.
CaseRealize.nothingMade: The realization placed nothing this chapter.
CaseRealize.undoAsk: Take back what the realization placed? Marked: {n}. What a student has found stays.
CaseRealize.askBody: A body was found. The case for this chapter has not been realized yet. Nothing happens until you choose.

CaseTrial.title: Case schema
CaseTrial.empty: No case schema yet. Build it on the Map in the Investigation panel.
CaseTrial.floorOpen: Another mode is running. End it first.
CaseTrial.hint: Hint: the evidence shown supports this

unknown.one: {n} presented card isn't on the schema.
unknown.other: {n} presented cards aren't on the schema.

CaseSummary.intro: Players get only this: what they found, the ticked deductions and counters, and the solution if they voted right.
CaseSummary.title: Chapter {chapter}: how the case was solved
CaseSummary.speaker: Case summary
CaseSummary.noSolution: The class voted wrong, so the solution stays hidden.

Reveal.title: Monokuma's Reveal
Reveal.intro: Everyone taking part in the trial receives {name} as a Key Remnant they found. Analyzing it costs what Analyze always costs.
Reveal.beyondPaid: No Despair was charged for this Key Remnant. Reveal it anyway?
Reveal.told: Monokuma reveals a Key Remnant you never found.
Reveal.notHydrated: The Key Remnant plan is still loading. Try again in a moment.
Reveal.notMissing: That Key Remnant is not missing: somebody found it, or Monokuma has revealed it.
Reveal.pastPaid: Every Key Remnant the Despair was charged for has been revealed. Confirm to reveal another.
Reveal.noText: Write what the players read on this Key Remnant first.
Reveal.notDone: The Key Remnant was not revealed.
